# PawConscious Mesh — Complete Engineering Documentation

> **Scope:** A single-file, exhaustive technical reference for the entire
> PawConscious Mesh codebase: every service, agent, shared library, protocol
> model, frontend surface, test, evaluation harness, build pipeline, deployment
> script, data corpus, and the demo/video production system. Part I is a
> structured reference; Part II is a full verbatim, line-annotated source
> walkthrough of every module.
>
> **System in one line:** A product URL goes in; a mesh of specialized Gemini
> agents on Google Cloud verifies each health claim, scores the evidence, checks
> FTC substantiation, and emits a cryptographically signed PCEC evidence bundle
> that any downstream AI shopping agent can trust over the A2A protocol.

# Part I — Structured Reference

## Architecture Overview

### System Overview

PawConscious Mesh is a multi-agent trust verification system for consumer pet product claims. It receives a product detail page (PDP) URL as input, runs a seven-agent verification pipeline grounded in peer-reviewed biomedical literature and regulatory corpora, and emits a signed PCEC v0.1 evidence bundle that downstream AI shopping agents can consume over the A2A v0.3 protocol.

**The end-to-end flow:**

1. A brand owner or AI shopping agent submits a product URL via `POST /a2a/v1/tasks/send` (A2A v0.3, JSON-RPC 2.0, async 202 lifecycle).
2. **Stage 1 — Reasoning mesh (5 agents):** The orchestrator runs the claim extractor first. For each extracted claim, three agents fan out in parallel via `asyncio.gather`: evidence grader (BioMCP/PubMed + Semantic Scholar), vet rubric (Gemini 2.5 Pro, 5-vet simulation), and compliance (Vertex AI Search over FTC §255 + AAFCO + NASC corpora). The auditor then runs a deterministic pre-sign pass on the merged per-claim evidence.
3. **Stage 2 — Signing:** The assembled `EndorsementClaimBundle` is canonicalized (RFC 8785-style, sort_keys + whole-float normalization), signed with Ed25519 against `did:web:<host>`, and appended to a public Firestore transparency log. The chain anchor is `sha256(bundle_hash + ":" + prev_chain_anchor)`, forming a verifiable append-only history.
4. **Stage 3 — Adversarial post-processing (2 agents):** A report writer (Cert Composer) renders an HTML certificate with an executive narrative. A second opinion agent runs four stress tests (COURT, REGULATOR, SCIENTIFIC CONSENSUS, PUBLIC SKEPTICISM) using Google Search grounding via `google.genai`. This pass fails closed on parse error; it can flip a verdict from PASS to NEEDS REVIEW based on live regulatory data (demonstrated: surfaced an FDA warning letter and the Cosequin $11.5M class-action precedent against a Native Pet product that initially scored PASS).
5. The signed bundle is returned to the polling caller via `GET /a2a/v1/tasks/get/{task_id}` and simultaneously resolvable at `GET /pcec/v0/claim/{urn}`.
6. Any A2A v0.3-compatible shopping agent (Amazon Rufus, Perplexity Shopping, Gemini Shopping, etc.) can discover the mesh via `GET /.well-known/agent-card.json` and call the `verify_claim` skill to obtain a trust score 0-1 plus the full PCEC bundle URN. The included ShopperAgent service demonstrates this end-to-end.

**Live deployment:** `https://mesh-api-40952019806.us-central1.run.app`  
**GCP project:** `pawconscious-mesh-2026` · region `us-central1`

## Request Lifecycle (numbered sequence)

The following describes the path of a `verify_claim` call from submission to result delivery.

1. **Discovery** — A downstream agent fetches `GET /.well-known/agent-card.json` and reads the `verify_claim` skill definition (input: product URL or SKU + claim text; output: trust score 0-1 + PCEC bundle URN).

2. **Task submission** — The caller sends `POST /a2a/v1/tasks/send` with `X-API-Key`, a JSON-RPC 2.0 envelope containing the product URL, and `skill: "verify_claim"`. `services/mesh_api/main.py` validates the API key, creates a task record in Firestore via `shared/task_store.py`, and returns `202 { task_id, poll_url, head_anchor_at_submit }`.

3. **Background dispatch** — The FastAPI background task invokes `agents/orchestrator.py::run_mesh(product_url)`.

4. **Claim extraction (Agent 1)** — `agents/claim_extractor.py::extract_claims()` fetches the PDP HTML via httpx + BeautifulSoup4, falling back to Firecrawl for bot-protected retailer PDPs. Gemini 2.5 Pro (`google.genai`, temperature=0) extracts a structured `Claim[]` — each claim carries `text`, `kind` (efficacy/safety/ingredient/expert/provenance/performance), and `position_on_page`.

5. **Parallel fan-out per claim (Agents 2, 3, 4)** — For each `Claim`, `asyncio.gather` fans out three coroutines simultaneously, each wrapped in an `agent_span` context manager that emits a structured Cloud Logging entry with `agent`, `duration_ms`, and `outcome` fields:

   - **Evidence grader** (`agents/evidence_grader.py`): Gemini 2.5 Pro extracts PubMed-suitable search terms, calls BioMCP (`biomcp.articles.search.search_articles`) which returns real PubMed PMIDs with abstracts, then Gemini grades each paper's `relevance_score` (0-1) and `supports_claim_direction` (bool). `agents/citation_enricher.py` batch-enriches every PMID with `citation_count` and `influential_citation_count` via the Semantic Scholar Graph API. Returns `EvidenceBundle`.

   - **Vet rubric** (`agents/vet_rubric.py`): Gemini 2.5 Pro simulates a 5-vet panel rubric (prompt-only, no licensed database). Returns `VetRubricScore` (1-5 scale) with an `escalate_to_human_vet` flag for ambiguous claims.

   - **Compliance** (`agents/compliance.py`): Gemini 2.5 Pro queries Vertex AI Search over the indexed FTC/AAFCO/NASC corpus. Returns `ComplianceMapping` with snippet-level `GroundingSource` objects, each carrying a `snippet_hash` (sha256) for tamper-evidence.

6. **Audit (Agent 5)** — `agents/auditor.py` (Gemini 2.5 Flash, Falsifier v0) receives the merged per-claim bundle and runs PMID format validation and claim-direction match checks. Returns `AuditVerdict` (PASS/FAIL/CONDITIONAL).

7. **Bundle assembly** — The orchestrator assembles the full `EndorsementClaimBundle` (Pydantic model per `shared/pcec_schema.py`), covering all claims with their evidence, vet scores, compliance mappings, and audit verdicts.

8. **Signing (mesh-api signing layer)** — `services/mesh_api/main.py` calls `shared/pcec_schema.py::canonical_bundle_bytes()` to produce the transport-stable canonical JSON bytes (sort_keys, whole-float normalization for RFC 8785 compatibility). The Ed25519 private key (loaded from Secret Manager) signs those bytes. The signature is embedded in the bundle.

9. **Transparency log append** — `shared/transparency_log.py` computes `chain_anchor = sha256(bundle_hash + ":" + prev_chain_anchor)` and appends the record to Firestore. If the append fails, `chain_anchor_status: "unavailable"` is set in the response — the caller never reads `null` as success.

10. **Report writing (Agent 6)** — `agents/report_writer.py` (Gemini 2.5 Pro) renders an HTML certificate: branded layout, 150-200-word executive narrative, and a "Ship before launch" list of actionable fixes keyed to specific claims.

11. **Second opinion (Agent 7)** — `agents/second_opinion.py` (Gemini 2.5 Pro + Google Search grounding) runs four adversarial stress tests against the signed bundle using real-time web evidence. Fails closed: a parse error produces a NEEDS REVIEW verdict rather than a silent pass. If the overall verdict is NEEDS REVIEW, the signed bundle is updated accordingly.

12. **Task completion** — The Firestore task record is updated to `status: "completed"` with the signed bundle, cert HTML, second opinion verdict, and chain anchor.

13. **Result retrieval** — The caller polls `GET /a2a/v1/tasks/get/{task_id}` until `status = "completed"`. Typical wall time: 2-4 minutes. The signed bundle is also permanently resolvable at `GET /pcec/v0/claim/{urn}`.

14. **Offline verification** — Any party can reproduce and verify the signature independently: fetch the bundle, recompute `canonical_bundle_bytes()`, fetch the Ed25519 public key from `GET /.well-known/did.json`, and call `verify()`. The entire transparency log history is readable at `GET /pcec/v0/chain/head`.

**Agent Engine routing (feature-flag path):** When `ACP_USE_AGENT_ENGINE=true`, step 3 routes through the deployed Vertex AI Reasoning Engine (`projects/40952019806/locations/us-central1/reasoningEngines/1255381144908595200`) using the ADK `ParallelAgent` + `SequentialAgent` wrappers declared in `agents/orchestrator.py`. A traffic gate auto-closes after three consecutive engine failures or if the engine p95 exceeds 2x the inline asyncio p95 over a 20-call rolling window. The env var is the manual kill switch.

## Governance and Safety Posture (NIST AI RMF)

PawConscious Mesh maps to NIST AI 100-1 (January 2023) and its 72-action Playbook. The assessment in `docs/NIST_AI_RMF_ASSESSMENT.md` documents 22 of 72 Playbook actions with shipped code evidence across all four functions.

**Why the framework applies with high severity:** The mesh is an LLM-driven multi-agent system producing signed verdicts that downstream agents act on autonomously, operating in a regulated domain (FTC §255, AAFCO PF7, NASC) with an active plaintiff-bar liability surface (Cosequin $11.5M settlement as the live template).

**Govern (5 actions satisfied):**
- Legal and regulatory requirements documented and operationalized in `agents/compliance.py` against public-redistributable corpus.
- Transparency enforced via public chain anchor, signed bundles, did:web identity, MIT license, and public agent card.
- Adversarial codex review after every major diff (8+ rounds over the 19-day build); findings absorbed before proceeding.
- Third-party risk (BioMCP, Semantic Scholar, Vertex AI Search, Firecrawl) documented in code comments with failure-mode handling.

**Map (6 actions satisfied):**
- Intended purpose, context, and applicable laws documented in `README.md` and `docs/PCEC-v0.md`.
- Human oversight path defined: `vet_rubric` returns `escalate_to_human_vet=true` on ambiguous claims.
- Single-issuer trust model at v0.1 stated explicitly; migration path to multi-issuer at v0.2 documented in `docs/INDEPENDENCE.md`.

**Measure (7 actions satisfied):**
- ADK Eval runner at `tests/adk_eval/run.py` with 4 structural assertions per case; timestamped results in `tests/adk_eval/results/`.
- Rolling p95 + consecutive-failure counter observable at `/health/agent-engine-traffic` without LLM invocation.
- Auditor explicitly scoped as **Falsifier v0** (PMID format + claim-direction only); limitations stated in code and cert HTML.
- Second opinion fails closed on parse error (MEASURE 2.6 — safety risks evaluated).
- Cloud Run timeout + circuit breaker + idempotency keys on A2A endpoint (MEASURE 2.7 — security and resilience).
- Every bundle carries `chain_anchor_status: "appended" | "unavailable"` — no silent failures (MEASURE 2.8).
- Every `ComplianceMapping` carries `grounding_sources` with `snippet_hash`; every `Evidence` has `relevance_score` + `supports_claim_direction` + free-text notes (MEASURE 2.9).

**Manage (4 actions satisfied):**
- Known P1/P2 issues documented in `internal/docs/FOLLOWUP_pre_flag_on.md`.
- Feature flag + traffic gate + circuit breaker allow safe deactivation of the Agent Engine path without redeployment (MANAGE 2.4).
- Health probes for all third-party dependencies: `/health/vertex-search`, `/health/agent-engine` (MANAGE 3.1).
- `chain_anchor_status: "unavailable"` propagated to calling agents when the log append fails (MANAGE 4.3).

**Honest gaps (8 documented):** No internal AI risk team (solo founder); no formal end-user feedback or appeal channel; no per-claim-kind bias audit; no token-usage telemetry; no formal privacy assessment for PDP content handling. All documented in `docs/NIST_AI_RMF_ASSESSMENT.md` §4.

## Glossary

**PCEC (Provenance for Commerce Endorsement Claims)**
The open JSON-LD schema and reference protocol published by PawConscious as a draft proposal (v0.1, CC-BY-4.0). Analogous to C2PA for images, but applied to expert endorsement claims on commerce surfaces. A PCEC bundle is the signed, verifiable artifact produced by the mesh for a single product's claims. One trust root at v0.1 (`did:web:mesh-api-40952019806.us-central1.run.app`). Linux Foundation donation is a stated forward path, not a v0.1 commitment.

**Mesh**
The seven-agent pipeline collectively. "Mesh" refers to the multi-agent reasoning topology (fan-out + merge + adversarial pass), not a service mesh in the Istio/Envoy sense.

**A2A (Agent-to-Agent protocol)**
Linux Foundation open protocol (v0.3, April 2026 GA). Defines agent card discovery via `/.well-known/agent-card.json`, JSON-RPC 2.0 task envelopes, and an async task lifecycle (submitted/working/completed/failed). Any A2A-compatible agent can discover and call the PawConscious Mesh without bespoke integration.

**ADK (Agent Development Kit)**
Google's open-source Python SDK for building Gemini-based agents. PawConscious uses `LlmAgent`, `FunctionTool`, `ParallelAgent`, and `SequentialAgent` primitives. The `ParallelAgent` + `SequentialAgent` wrappers in `agents/orchestrator.py` are the declared deployment surface for the Vertex AI Agent Engine (Reasoning Engine) path.

**Claim**
One atomic assertion extracted from a product detail page — e.g., "Supports joint mobility in senior dogs." Each claim carries a `kind` (efficacy/safety/ingredient/expert/provenance/performance), position on page, and raw surrounding context. Claims are the unit of analysis through the full pipeline.

**Evidence bundle**
The set of peer-reviewed papers retrieved and graded for a single claim. Each paper entry includes its PMID, DOI, `relevance_score` (0-1), `citation_count`, `influential_citation_count`, and a `supports_claim_direction` boolean. The bundle is produced by the evidence grader agent using BioMCP/PubMed + Semantic Scholar enrichment.

**Chain anchor**
The per-bundle value that links the transparency log into a verifiable history: `sha256(bundle_hash + ":" + prev_chain_anchor)`. The genesis anchor uses the string `"genesis"` as the previous value. Anyone can verify the entire log offline by recomputing the chain from the first entry. The current head is public at `GET /pcec/v0/chain/head`.

**Second opinion**
Agent 7. Runs after the bundle is signed. Executes four adversarial stress tests (COURT, REGULATOR, SCIENTIFIC CONSENSUS, PUBLIC SKEPTICISM) using real-time Google Search grounding. Can flip a PASS verdict to NEEDS REVIEW based on live evidence (regulatory actions, plaintiff cases, scientific consensus shifts). Fails closed on parse error — no silent passes.

**Vet rubric**
Agent 3 (`agents/vet_rubric.py`). A Gemini 2.5 Pro simulation of a 5-vet panel scoring each claim on a 1-5 scale. This is a prompt-only rubric simulation, not licensed DVM attestation. The `escalate_to_human_vet` flag surfaces ambiguous claims for human review. Renamed from "vet-panel" in v0.10.1a after a honesty audit (the field is a rubric score, not a panel verdict). Licensed DVM attestation is the `attest_expert` A2A skill on the v0.2 roadmap.

**Auditor (Falsifier v0)**
Agent 5 (`agents/auditor.py`). A deterministic pre-sign pass using Gemini 2.5 Flash. Checks PMID format validity and claim-direction match (does the cited paper support or contradict the claim?). Labeled v0 because cherry-pick detection and sample-size adequacy checks are post-hackathon. The second opinion's adversarial pass catches what the auditor misses.

**did:web**
A DID (Decentralized Identifier) method that resolves via HTTPS. The PawConscious issuer DID `did:web:mesh-api-40952019806.us-central1.run.app` resolves to `GET /.well-known/did.json`, which contains the Ed25519 verification public key. This allows any party to verify a signed bundle without trusting PawConscious's API — only the DNS/TLS root.

**Vertex AI Agent Engine / Reasoning Engine**
Google Cloud managed runtime for ADK agents. PawConscious deploys the orchestrator as a Reasoning Engine and routes traffic to it via the `ACP_USE_AGENT_ENGINE` feature flag. The route is gated by a rolling p95 traffic gate and a three-consecutive-failure circuit breaker; the fallback is the inline `asyncio.gather` path. Resource: `projects/40952019806/locations/us-central1/reasoningEngines/1255381144908595200`.

**BioMCP**
Open-source Model Context Protocol server for biomedical literature (MIT license, `biomcp-python>=0.7.0`). Provides 21 PubMed/Europe PMC search and retrieval tools. The evidence grader calls it via Python library import in v0.1; the MCP stdio protocol path is in `agents/evidence_grader_mcp.py` for future full MCP compliance.

**ShopperAgent**
A separate Cloud Run service (`services/shopper_agent/`) that demonstrates external A2A consumption of the mesh. It accepts shopping intent ("best joint supplement for senior labs"), fetches the PawConscious agent card, calls `verify_claim` via A2A v0.3, and returns a ranked product list with trust scores. Its source is public so judges can verify the external A2A call is real, not staged.

## Pipeline Overview

The PawConscious Mesh is an asynchronous multi-agent pipeline that verifies the health and efficacy claims made by direct-to-consumer pet supplement brands. Given a product detail page (PDP) URL, it:

1. **Extracts** every health/efficacy claim from the page (Claim Extractor, Agent 1).
2. **Fans out** three parallel checks per claim:
   - Retrieves and grades peer-reviewed PubMed evidence (Evidence Grader, Agent 2).
   - Simulates a five-veterinarian rubric score (Vet Rubric, Agent 3).
   - Maps each claim to FTC §255, AAFCO PF7, and NASC standards (Compliance, Agent 4).
3. **Enriches** raw PubMed citations with influence metrics from Semantic Scholar (Citation Enricher, Agent 5 — called from within Agent 2, not from the orchestrator directly).
4. **Audits** the assembled evidence bundle adversarially for PMID format validity and claim-direction consistency (Auditor, Agent 6).
5. **Composes** a signed HTML verification certificate from the completed bundle (Report Writer / Cert Composer, Agent 7).
6. **Stress-tests** the entire bundle with four adversarial probes using Google Search grounding (Second Opinion, Agent 8).
7. **Ingests** optional third-party lab documents (COA Ingester, Agent 9 — invoked separately from the main pipeline).

The Orchestrator wraps steps 1–4 in `asyncio.gather` fan-out and assembles the final `EndorsementClaimBundle`. The Report Writer and Second Opinion are invoked downstream in the API layer after bundle signing.

**4 of 7 primary mesh agents are declared on ADK**: `acp_claim_extractor` (Agent 1), `acp_evidence_grader` (Agent 2), `acp_compliance` (Agent 4), and `acp_auditor` (Agent 6). The runtime execution path uses `asyncio.gather` fan-out for determinism and debuggability; the ADK objects are real and introspectable via `/health/mesh-shape`.

## Shared Data Models

**File:** `shared/pcec_schema.py`

All inter-agent data is typed using Pydantic v2 `BaseModel` classes under the PCEC v0.1 schema. Every agent consumes and/or produces one or more of these models.

### `ClaimKind` (Enum, line 52)

```python
class ClaimKind(str, Enum):
    EFFICACY = "efficacy"
    SAFETY = "safety"
    INGREDIENT = "ingredient"
    EXPERT = "expert"
    PROVENANCE = "provenance"
    PERFORMANCE = "performance"
```

String enum used to classify extracted claims. The string value is passed verbatim into LLM prompts.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `claim` | `Claim` | The claim mapped |
| `ftc_section` | `Optional[str]` | E.g., `"16 CFR §255.3"` |

### `AuditVerdict` (BaseModel, line 115)

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `claim` | `Claim` | The claim audited |
| `verdict` | `str` | `PASS` / `FAIL` / `CONDITIONAL` |
| `challenges_run` | `list[str]` | List of check names run (always includes `direction_only_falsifier_v0`) |
| `findings` | `list[str]` | Human-readable list of issues found |
| `auditor_agent` | `str` | DID of the auditor agent |

### `EndorsementClaimBundle` (BaseModel, line 124)

The top-level output of the entire mesh pipeline.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `sku` | `str` | Product identifier (v0.1 uses the URL as SKU) |
| `product_url` | `str` | The PDP URL that was analyzed |
| `claims` | `list[Claim]` | All extracted claims |
| `evidence` | `list[EvidenceBundle]` | One bundle per claim |
| `vet_scores` | `list[VetRubricScore]` | One score per claim |
| `compliance` | `list[ComplianceMapping]` | One mapping per claim |
| `audit` | `list[AuditVerdict]` | One verdict per claim |
| `issued_at` | `datetime` | UTC timestamp |
| `issuer` | `str` | DID of the mesh API |
| `bundle_urn` | `Optional[str]` | Derived from bundle hash after signing |
| `signature` | `Optional[str]` | Ed25519 signature (excluded from signed bytes) |

### `canonical_bundle_bytes` (function, line 13)

**Signature:** `canonical_bundle_bytes(obj: Any) -> bytes`

Produces transport-stable canonical bytes for signing and hashing. Accepts either an `EndorsementClaimBundle` instance or a plain dict. Excludes `signature` and `bundle_urn` from the serialized form (the former cannot sign itself; the latter is derived after hashing). Applies number canonicalization: whole-valued floats are collapsed to ints so that Python's JSON emission (`1.0`) matches JavaScript's (`1`) for client-side verification. Serializes with `sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")`.

## Shared Infrastructure

### `shared/llm_retry.py`

**`with_retry`** (async, line 15):

```python
async def with_retry(fn, *, max_attempts=3, initial_delay=1.0, max_delay=8.0, timeout_seconds=60.0) -> T
```

Wraps any async callable with exponential backoff retry. Catches `ResourceExhausted`, `DeadlineExceeded`, `ServiceUnavailable`, and `InternalServerError` by exception class name (string matching for Google API compatibility). Retries up to `max_attempts` with a doubling delay capped at `max_delay`. Each attempt is hard-limited by `asyncio.wait_for` with `timeout_seconds=60`. Non-transient exceptions are re-raised immediately without retry.

**`agenerate`** (async, line 53):

```python
async def agenerate(client, **kwargs)
```

Offloads the blocking `client.models.generate_content(**kwargs)` call to a thread pool via `asyncio.to_thread`. This prevents a single Gemini call from blocking the event loop and freezing other in-flight requests (including task-poll endpoints). Does not itself retry; callers that need retry must wrap with `with_retry`.

### `shared/telemetry.py`

**`agent_span`** (async context manager, line 62):

```python
@asynccontextmanager
async def agent_span(agent: str, *, claim_id: str | None = None, extra: dict | None = None) -> AsyncIterator[None]
```

Times an agent call and emits a single JSON line to stdout (routed to Cloud Logging by Cloud Run). The record includes `span_name`, `agent`, optional `claim_id`, optional `task_id` (from a contextvar set by the API layer), `outcome` (`ok` or `error`), and `duration_ms`. On exception, the record is emitted with `outcome=error` plus `error_type` and `error_message` (truncated to 240 chars), then the exception is re-raised. Used by the Orchestrator to wrap each agent call site.

**`set_task_id`** (line 44): Binds a task ID to the current async context via a `contextvars.ContextVar` so all spans within a verify task share the same correlation ID without modifying every call signature.

**`log_route_decision`** (line 106): Emits a `route_decision` span line when the API layer decides to route traffic via Agent Engine or inline asyncio.

## Agent 1 — Claim Extractor

**File:** `agents/claim_extractor.py`

**Pipeline stage:** Step 1 (sequential, before fan-out). The entry point of the mesh.

**Purpose:** Fetches a product detail page URL and extracts every health/efficacy claim using Gemini 2.5 Pro reasoning. Returns a `list[Claim]` structured per PCEC v0.1. Is one of the 4 agents declared on ADK as `acp_claim_extractor` (ADK type: `LlmAgent` with a `FunctionTool`).

### SSRF Guard Functions

The agent fetches an attacker-controlled URL server-side on Cloud Run. A naïve fetch can reach the GCP metadata server (`169.254.169.254`) for service-account token exfiltration.

**`_assert_public_url(url: str) -> None`** (line 33)

Validates a URL before any network call. Raises `ValueError` for:
- Non-http(s) schemes.
- Hostnames in `_BLOCKED_HOSTS = {"metadata.google.internal", "metadata", "localhost"}`.
- Empty hostnames.
- Hostnames that resolve to private, loopback, link-local, reserved, multicast, or unspecified IP addresses (checked via `socket.getaddrinfo` + `ipaddress.ip_address`).

**`_ssrf_guarded_get(client, url, headers, max_redirects=5) -> httpx.Response`** (async, line 54)

Manually follows HTTP redirects (up to `max_redirects`) so that `_assert_public_url` is called on **every hop**, not just the initial URL. A redirect from a public host to a private IP would otherwise bypass the guard. Returns when a non-redirect response is received. Raises `ValueError` on exceeding `max_redirects`.

### Firecrawl Fallback

**`_load_firecrawl_key() -> str | None`** (line 89)

Loads the Firecrawl API key from the `FIRECRAWL_API_KEY` environment variable or, failing that, from Google Secret Manager at `projects/pawconscious-mesh-2026/secrets/acp-firecrawl-key/versions/latest`. Returns `None` on any failure (broad `Exception` catch is intentional; documented). Prints the failure class and message rather than silently swallowing.

**`_fetch_via_firecrawl(url: str) -> str`** (async, line 110)

Calls the Firecrawl `/v2/scrape` endpoint (`POST https://api.firecrawl.dev/v2/scrape`) with `formats=["markdown"]` and `onlyMainContent=True`. Returns the cleaned markdown content, truncated to 20,000 characters. Raises `RuntimeError` if the key is not configured or if Firecrawl returns no markdown.

### Primary Fetch

**`fetch_pdp_html(url: str) -> str`** (async, line 137)

**Parameters:** `url` — product detail page URL.  
**Returns:** Cleaned text content (up to 20,000 chars).

Two-path strategy:

1. **httpx + BeautifulSoup (primary):** Sends a real browser `User-Agent` header. Uses `_ssrf_guarded_get` with `follow_redirects=False`. On a successful response, parses HTML with `lxml`, strips `<script>`, `<style>`, `<noscript>`, `<nav>`, `<footer>`, `<header>` tags, extracts text from `<main>` or `[role=main]` or `<body>`. If the extracted text is under 400 characters (anti-bot block page heuristic), falls back to Firecrawl.

2. **Firecrawl (fallback):** Triggered on HTTP 403, 429, or 503, network errors (`httpx.ConnectError`, `httpx.TimeoutException`), or thin body. Handles Akamai/Cloudflare/PerimeterX anti-bot for retailers like Chewy and Petco. **SSRF-guard rejections do not fall back** — they raise immediately (line 161).

### Prompt

**`CLAIM_EXTRACTION_PROMPT`** (module-level string, line 190)

Injected at line 266 via `.format(pdp_text=pdp_text)`. System role: claim-extractor agent in the PawConscious Mesh. User content: PDP text.

Key instructions:
- Extract every statement implying a specific health, behavioral, or physiological effect.
- Classify by kind (`efficacy`, `safety`, `ingredient`, `expert`, `provenance`, `performance`).
- Record position on page and surrounding context.
- Be **exhaustive** (subtle implied claims) and **honest** (no invented claims).
- Return strict JSON: `{"claims": [{"text": ..., "kind": ..., "position_on_page": ..., "raw_context": ...}]}`.

The prompt explicitly warns against inventing claims and requires returning an empty list with an explanation if none are found.

### ADK Agent Declaration

**`build_claim_extractor_agent() -> LlmAgent`** (line 232)

Constructs the ADK `LlmAgent` for the claim extractor. Returns a fresh instance each call (cached once into the orchestrator topology to avoid ADK single-parent re-assignment errors).

```
LlmAgent(
    name="claim_extractor",
    model="gemini-2.5-pro",
    tools=[FunctionTool(fetch_pdp_html)],
    instruction="When called with a product URL, use the fetch_pdp_html tool..."
)
```

The `FunctionTool` wrapping `fetch_pdp_html` makes the SSRF-guarded fetch available to the ADK runtime.

### Runtime Path

**`extract_claims(url: str) -> list[Claim]`** (async, line 253)

Used by the orchestrator's runtime path (not the ADK runner). Calls `fetch_pdp_html`, then calls Gemini 2.5 Pro directly via `agenerate` with `response_mime_type="application/json"` and `temperature=0.0`. Parses the JSON response handling both `{"claims": [...]}` and bare list responses. Maps `kind` strings to `ClaimKind` enum values, defaulting to `ClaimKind.EFFICACY` on unknown values.

**External calls:**
- `httpx` — PDP fetch (primary path).
- `Firecrawl API` — PDP fetch (fallback, conditional).
- `Google Secret Manager` — Firecrawl key retrieval (conditional).
- `Gemini 2.5 Pro` via Vertex AI (`pawconscious-mesh-2026`, `us-central1`) — claim extraction reasoning.

---

## Agent 2 — Evidence Grader

**File:** `agents/evidence_grader.py`

**Pipeline stage:** Step 2, parallel branch 1 (runs concurrently with Vet Rubric and Compliance per claim). Is one of the 4 agents declared on ADK as `acp_evidence_grader`.

**Purpose:** For each `Claim`, extracts PubMed search terms using Gemini, queries PubMed via BioMCP, grades each paper's relevance and support direction via Gemini, then enriches citation counts via Semantic Scholar. Returns an `EvidenceBundle` with real PMIDs and influence scores.

### Prompts

**`KEYWORD_EXTRACTION_PROMPT`** (line 32)

Injected at `extract_search_terms` with `claim_text` and `claim_kind`. Instructs Gemini to extract:
- `keywords`: 3–6 PubMed-suitable keyword strings (combine "dog" or "canine" for pet-specific claims).
- `chemicals`: specific compounds (chondroitin, glucosamine, MSM, turmeric, omega-3, curcumin).
- `diseases`: condition terms (osteoarthritis, joint mobility, anxiety, dermatitis).

Return format: `{"keywords": [...], "chemicals": [...], "diseases": [...]}`. Emphasizes specificity over generic terms.

**`GRADING_PROMPT`** (line 56)

Injected at `grade_evidence` with `claim_text`, `claim_kind`, and `search_results`. Instructs Gemini to grade each paper with a real PMID by:
- `relevance_score`: 0.0–1.0 directness of relevance.
- `supports_claim_direction`: true if the paper supports what the claim asserts.
- `notes`: one-sentence rationale.

Critical constraint: **Do NOT invent PMIDs. Only use PMIDs visible in the search results.** Returns `{"papers": [...]}`.

### Functions

**`_client() -> genai.Client`** (line 82)

Returns a Vertex AI Gemini client for project `pawconscious-mesh-2026`, location `us-central1`.

**`extract_search_terms(claim: Claim) -> dict[str, list[str]]`** (async, line 86)

**Parameters:** `claim` — the `Claim` to analyze.  
**Returns:** `{"keywords": [...], "chemicals": [...], "diseases": [...]}`.

Calls Gemini 2.5 Pro with `KEYWORD_EXTRACTION_PROMPT` via `agenerate`. Response MIME type is `application/json`. Temperature is `0.0`.

**`search_pubmed(claim: Claim, limit: int = 10, debug: bool = False) -> str`** (async, line 109)

**Parameters:** `claim`, `limit` (max results), `debug` (verbose logging).  
**Returns:** BioMCP search results as a markdown text blob.

Calls `extract_search_terms`, then caps each dimension to 2 terms (`keywords[:2]`, `chemicals[:2]`, `diseases[:2]`) because PubMed AND-joins all terms — too many terms produce empty results. Constructs a `PubmedRequest` and calls `biomcp.articles.search.search_articles`. BioMCP's `search_articles` returns markdown text, not JSON.

**`grade_evidence(claim: Claim, search_results: str, debug: bool = False) -> list[Evidence]`** (async, line 134)

**Parameters:** `claim`, `search_results` (BioMCP markdown blob, capped to 15,000 chars in prompt), `debug`.  
**Returns:** `list[Evidence]`.

Returns an empty list if `search_results` is under 50 characters. Calls Gemini 2.5 Pro with `GRADING_PROMPT` via `agenerate`. Validates each PMID against `PMID_REGEX = re.compile(r"\b\d{6,9}\b")` — invalid PMIDs are dropped. Constructs `Evidence` objects with `citation_count=0` and `influential_citation_count=0` (pre-enrichment defaults).

**`grade_claim(claim: Claim, debug: bool = False) -> EvidenceBundle`** (async, line 191)

End-to-end entry point for the orchestrator's runtime path. Calls:
1. `search_pubmed(claim)` → BioMCP markdown.
2. `grade_evidence(claim, search_results)` → `list[Evidence]`.
3. `enrich_with_citations(papers)` (from `agents.citation_enricher`) → enriched `list[Evidence]`.
4. Returns `EvidenceBundle(claim=claim, papers=papers, grader_run_id=None)`.

**External calls:**
- `BioMCP` (`biomcp.articles.search.search_articles`) — PubMed search.
- `Gemini 2.5 Pro` via Vertex AI — keyword extraction + evidence grading.
- `Semantic Scholar Graph API` — citation enrichment (via `citation_enricher`).

### ADK Agent Declaration

**`search_pubmed_for_adk(keywords, chemicals, diseases, max_results=8) -> str`** (async, line 218)

ADK `FunctionTool` entry point. Takes pre-extracted terms (the typed output of the keyword-extraction step) and calls BioMCP's `search_articles`. Returns BioMCP's response as a string (markdown text). Handles the case where a future BioMCP version returns a list/dict by JSON-serializing it, ensuring the ADK LlmAgent always receives a string. **Does not call `json.loads`** on the BioMCP result (a prior bug that caused `JSONDecodeError` since BioMCP returns markdown, not JSON).

**`evidence_grader_adk`** (module-level `LlmAgent` instance, line 263)

```
LlmAgent(
    name="acp_evidence_grader",
    model="gemini-2.5-pro",
    tools=[FunctionTool(search_pubmed_for_adk)],
    output_key="evidence_bundle",
    instruction=EVIDENCE_GRADER_ADK_INSTRUCTION,
)
```

Instruction (line 248): Three ordered steps — (1) extract keywords/chemicals/diseases from claim; (2) call `search_pubmed_for_adk` tool (returns markdown text, parse as text not JSON); (3) grade each paper for relevance + direction + notes. Return JSON matching `EvidenceBundle` schema. Never invent PMIDs.

## Agent 2-MCP — Evidence Grader via MCP Protocol

**File:** `agents/evidence_grader_mcp.py`

**Pipeline stage:** Alternative implementation of Agent 2. Not invoked by the default orchestrator runtime; introduced in Phase 3.5 for A2A MCP compliance.

**Purpose:** Replaces the direct Python import of `biomcp` with proper MCP protocol usage — spawning `biomcp run --mode stdio` as a subprocess and communicating via `mcp.client.stdio.stdio_client`. This satisfies the A2A public-facing endpoint's MCP compliance promise. The original `evidence_grader.py` is preserved as fallback if the MCP subprocess fails during demo.

### Key Items

**`BIOMCP_SERVER_PARAMS`** (line 35)

```python
StdioServerParameters(command="biomcp", args=["run", "--mode", "stdio"])
```

Parameters for spawning the BioMCP MCP server as a subprocess.

**`biomcp_session()`** (async context manager, line 41)

Spawns `biomcp` as a subprocess using `mcp.client.stdio.stdio_client`, opens an `mcp.ClientSession`, and calls `session.initialize()`. Yields the initialized session.

**`search_pubmed_via_mcp(claim: Claim, limit: int = 10, debug: bool = False) -> str`** (async, line 50)

Calls `extract_search_terms` (from `agents.evidence_grader`) to get search terms, caps each dimension to 2, then:
1. Opens a `biomcp_session`.
2. Calls `session.list_tools()` to discover available tools dynamically.
3. Identifies the article search tool by checking candidates `("article_searcher", "search_articles", "article_search")`, then falling back to partial-name matching on `"article"` + `"search"`.
4. Calls `session.call_tool(search_tool, arguments={...})` with the capped terms and `limit`.
5. Concatenates text content from all MCP response items.

**`grade_claim_via_mcp(claim: Claim, debug: bool = False) -> EvidenceBundle`** (async, line 106)

End-to-end via MCP. Calls `search_pubmed_via_mcp`, then calls `grade_evidence` (from `agents.evidence_grader`) on the result, then calls `enrich_with_citations`. Sets `grader_agent` to the MCP-variant DID (`...evidence-grader-mcp`).

**Imports from `agents.evidence_grader`:** `GRADING_PROMPT`, `KEYWORD_EXTRACTION_PROMPT`, `PMID_REGEX`, `extract_search_terms`, `grade_evidence` — does not duplicate that logic.

**External calls:**
- `biomcp` subprocess — spawned as an MCP stdio server.
- `mcp` SDK — `ClientSession`, `StdioServerParameters`, `stdio_client`.
- `Gemini 2.5 Pro` via Vertex AI — via imported `extract_search_terms` and `grade_evidence`.
- `Semantic Scholar Graph API` — via `enrich_with_citations`.

## Agent 3 — Vet Rubric

**File:** `agents/vet_rubric.py`

**Pipeline stage:** Step 2, parallel branch 2 (runs concurrently with Evidence Grader and Compliance per claim).

**Purpose:** Simulates a panel of five board-certified veterinarians (DVM with ACVN or ACVIM specialty) scoring a claim on a 1–5 rubric. Returns a `VetRubricScore` including an average score, rationale, and escalation flag. **This is an LLM simulation, not a real veterinary panel.** The production roadmap routes high-stakes claims to a real vet panel (Phase 3+ manual attestation). This agent flags those claims for escalation via `escalate_to_human_vet`. This agent is **not on ADK** (locked Day-19 decision; stays on direct `genai`).

### Prompt

**`VET_RUBRIC_PROMPT`** (line 28)

System role: simulating a panel of 5 board-certified vets. Injected with `claim_text`, `claim_kind`, and `claim_context`.

Rubric definition:
- `5` — strong RCT evidence in target species, clear mechanism, real clinical magnitude.
- `4` — moderate evidence (smaller studies or related species), plausible mechanism.
- `3` — mixed or limited evidence, mechanism plausible but not proven.
- `2` — sparse evidence, weak mechanism, mostly extrapolation.
- `1` — no peer-reviewed evidence supporting the claim direction; promotional language.

Escalation rule encoded in prompt: `escalate_to_human_vet: true` if score ≤ 3 OR if the claim involves clinical disease management (e.g., "treats arthritis", "prevents infection").

Returns: `{"score": <int 1-5>, "rationale": "...", "escalate_to_human_vet": <bool>}`.

### Functions

**`_client() -> genai.Client`** (line 56): Returns Vertex AI Gemini client for `pawconscious-mesh-2026`.

**`score_claim(claim: Claim) -> VetRubricScore`** (async, line 60)

**Parameters:** `claim` — the `Claim` to score.  
**Returns:** `VetRubricScore`.

Calls Gemini 2.5 Pro with `VET_RUBRIC_PROMPT` via `agenerate`. Temperature is `0.0`. Clamps the returned score to `[1, 5]`. Constructs `VetRubricScore(claim=claim, score=score, rationale=..., escalate_to_human_vet=...)`.

**External calls:**
- `Gemini 2.5 Pro` via Vertex AI — rubric scoring.

No ADK object declared for this agent. Not in the ADK topology's `sub_agents` lists.

## Agent 4 — Compliance

**File:** `agents/compliance.py`

**Pipeline stage:** Step 2, parallel branch 3 (runs concurrently with Evidence Grader and Vet Rubric per claim). Is one of the 4 agents declared on ADK as `acp_compliance`.

**Purpose:** Maps each claim to public-redistributable US regulatory language via Vertex AI Search RAG over a corpus of FTC 16 CFR §255 (Endorsement Guides 2023 update), AAFCO PF7 substantiation, and NASC Quality Seal public-side requirements. Returns a `ComplianceMapping` with grounded provenance via `GroundingSource` objects. No licensed handbooks are ingested.

**Corpus:** `projects/40952019806/locations/global/.../acp-regulator-corpus` (Vertex AI Search datastore, serving config `default_serving_config`).

### Prompt

**`COMPLIANCE_PROMPT`** (line 31)

Injected at `map_claim` with `claim_text`, `claim_kind`, and `claim_context`, prepended by the grounding block from Vertex AI Search retrieval (or a `"(grounding unavailable — using prompt-only knowledge)"` marker if retrieval fails).

Instructs Gemini to map the claim to:
- `ftc_section`: applicable §255 subsection or `"none"`.
- `aafco_definition`: applicable AAFCO definition or `"none"`.
- `nasc_public_standard`: applicable NASC requirement or `"none"`.
- `violation_flag`: true if the claim would likely fail §255 substantiation.
- `rationale`: 1–2 sentences explaining the mapping.

The prompt encodes summaries of FTC §255.3 (expert endorser credentials + exercise of expertise), §255.2 (consumer endorsement typicality + substantiation), §255.1 (general deceptive endorsement prohibition), AAFCO PF7 claim substantiation rules (vet-recommended survey requirement, vet-formulated documentation), and NASC public-side requirements (biennial audit, SOPs, AER system, random testing — explicitly noting NASC does NOT certify clinical efficacy).

### Functions

**`_client() -> genai.Client`** (line 75): Returns Vertex AI Gemini client for `pawconscious-mesh-2026`.

**`_search_data_store_path() -> str`** (line 79): Returns the full Vertex AI Search serving config resource path.

**`retrieve_grounding_sources(claim: Claim, max_results: int = 5) -> list[GroundingSource]`** (async, line 87)

**Parameters:** `claim`, `max_results`.  
**Returns:** `list[GroundingSource]` (may be empty on any retrieval failure).

Uses the **manual retrieval pattern** — calls Vertex AI Search directly via `google.cloud.discoveryengine.SearchServiceClient` rather than using the Gemini `vertex_ai_search` tool. Reason: Gemini's `vertex_ai_search` Tool is incompatible with `response_mime_type="application/json"` (controlled generation). The manual pattern retrieves passages, injects them into the prompt, and then calls Gemini in JSON mode.

Query construction: `f"{claim.text} {claim.kind.value} endorsement substantiation"`.

Extracts snippets from `derived_struct_data` in priority order: `snippets` → `extractive_answers` → `extractive_segments`. Uses `snippet_spec` only (Standard tier; extractive features require Enterprise). Each retrieved snippet becomes a `GroundingSource(source_id=title, snippet=snippet[:500], snippet_hash=f"sha256:{sha256_hex16}")`.

On any exception (broad catch is intentional — Vertex AI Search can raise `NotFound`, `PermissionDenied`, `DeadlineExceeded`, `ResourceExhausted`, transient gRPC errors), returns empty list and falls back to prompt-only mode at the caller. Never silently swallowed: prints `[compliance] retrieval failed:` with the exception class and message.

**`map_claim(claim: Claim) -> ComplianceMapping`** (async, line 224)

End-to-end entry point used by the orchestrator's runtime path.

1. Calls `retrieve_grounding_sources(claim)`.
2. If sources found: prepends a `"GROUNDED REGULATORY PASSAGES"` block to the prompt with source IDs, hashes, and snippets.
3. If no sources: prepends `"(grounding unavailable — using prompt-only knowledge)"`.
4. Calls Gemini 2.5 Pro with the assembled prompt via `agenerate`, `temperature=0.0`, `response_mime_type="application/json"`.
5. Constructs `ComplianceMapping` from the JSON response, converting `"none"` strings to `None` for optional fields.

**Returns:** `ComplianceMapping` with `grounding_sources` populated.

### ADK Agent Declaration

**`retrieve_grounding_sources_for_adk(claim_text, claim_kind, max_results=5) -> str`** (async, line 174)

ADK `FunctionTool` entry point. Constructs a temporary `Claim` from the string arguments, calls `retrieve_grounding_sources`, and returns JSON-serialized list of `{source_id, snippet, snippet_hash}` dicts. Returns JSON (not markdown) because Vertex AI Search returns structured passages.

**`compliance_adk`** (module-level `LlmAgent` instance, line 210)

```
LlmAgent(
    name="acp_compliance",
    model="gemini-2.5-pro",
    tools=[FunctionTool(retrieve_grounding_sources_for_adk)],
    output_key="compliance_mapping",
    instruction=COMPLIANCE_ADK_INSTRUCTION,
)
```

Instruction (line 196): Two ordered steps — (1) call the tool with claim text + kind to get FTC §255 + AAFCO PF7 + NASC passages; (2) map the claim and return `ComplianceMapping` JSON. Mark `§255` violation only for clinical disease language without support.

**External calls:**
- `Vertex AI Search` (`google.cloud.discoveryengine`) — regulatory corpus retrieval.
- `Gemini 2.5 Pro` via Vertex AI — compliance mapping reasoning.

## Agent 5 — Citation Enricher

**File:** `agents/citation_enricher.py`

**Pipeline stage:** Called from within `agents/evidence_grader.py:grade_claim` (line 198), not directly by the orchestrator. Runs after BioMCP search and Gemini grading, before returning the `EvidenceBundle`.

**Purpose:** Enriches a list of `Evidence` objects with real `citation_count` and `influential_citation_count` values from AI2's Semantic Scholar Graph API batch endpoint. This agent involves no LLM — it is a pure HTTP enrichment step. The interface is kept narrow (one async function, list in → list out) so an MCP wrapper is a drop-in if AI2 ships an "Asta MCP" server.

**API endpoint:** `POST https://api.semanticscholar.org/graph/v1/paper/batch?fields=citationCount,influentialCitationCount`

**Batch limit:** 500 PMIDs per call. **Timeout:** 10.0 seconds. **Auth:** Optional `SEMANTIC_SCHOLAR_API_KEY` environment variable; without it, uses the public anonymous tier (1 req/sec shared pool — batch is safer than single-paper endpoints).

### Functions

**`enrich_with_citations(papers: list[Evidence], *, debug: bool = False) -> list[Evidence]`** (async, line 44)

**Parameters:** `papers` — list of `Evidence` objects with `pmid` fields.  
**Returns:** New list of `Evidence` with `citation_count` and `influential_citation_count` populated where possible. On any error, returns the input list unchanged (counts stay at 0). Never raises.

Implementation:
1. Deduplicates PMIDs preserving first-seen order.
2. Batches up to `S2_MAX_BATCH = 500` PMIDs per HTTP call using `f"PMID:{pmid}"` format IDs.
3. On non-200 response: logs and returns the input unchanged.
4. On `httpx.HTTPError` or `ValueError`: logs and returns input unchanged.
5. Builds `counts: dict[str, tuple[int, int]]` mapping PMID to `(citationCount, influentialCitationCount)`.
6. Uses `p.model_copy(update={...})` to produce enriched copies (Pydantic v2 pattern).

**Side effects:** None. Does not mutate input Evidence objects. On debug=True, logs the count of papers that received non-zero citation counts.

**External calls:**
- `Semantic Scholar Graph API` — one HTTP POST per batch of ≤500 PMIDs.

## Agent 6 — Auditor

**File:** `agents/auditor.py`

**Pipeline stage:** Step 3 (sequential, after parallel fan-out). Runs per claim after the Evidence Grader returns an `EvidenceBundle`. Is one of the 4 agents declared on ADK as `acp_auditor`.

**Purpose:** Adversarial falsifier (labeled `v0` in all outputs). Runs two checks on each `EvidenceBundle`: PMID format validation and claim-direction consistency. Returns an `AuditVerdict` with a `PASS`, `FAIL`, or `CONDITIONAL` verdict and a list of findings. Full cherry-pick detection, sample-size adequacy, and statistical-significance checks are post-hackathon scope (codex G7.3).

### Prompt

**`AUDIT_PROMPT`** (line 37)

Injected with `claim_text`, `claim_kind`, and `evidence_json` (serialized Evidence list). System role: adversarial auditor agent.

Two checks:
1. **Citation existence:** every PMID must be a valid PubMed ID format (6–9 digits).
2. **Claim direction match:** for each paper with `supports_claim_direction=true`, the `notes` rationale must actually support the claim — not contradict it or describe a different mechanism.

Verdict logic encoded in prompt:
- `PASS` — all PMIDs valid, all directions match.
- `CONDITIONAL` — some valid evidence + at least one fixable issue.
- `FAIL` — no valid evidence OR every direction mismatched.

Prompt instructs: "Be RUTHLESS." Returns `{"verdict": ..., "challenges_run": [...], "findings": [...]}`.

### Functions

**`_client() -> genai.Client`** (line 70): Returns Vertex AI Gemini client for `pawconscious-mesh-2026`.

**`audit_bundle(bundle: EvidenceBundle) -> AuditVerdict`** (async, line 74)

**Parameters:** `bundle` — the `EvidenceBundle` to audit.  
**Returns:** `AuditVerdict`.

Pre-flight PMID format check (no LLM, line 79): scans all papers against `PMID_REGEX = re.compile(r"\A\d{6,9}\Z")` — a stricter anchored regex than the one in `evidence_grader.py`.

If `bundle.papers` is empty (line 81): returns a `FAIL` verdict immediately without calling the LLM.

Otherwise, serializes the evidence to JSON and calls Gemini 2.5 **Flash** (cheaper/faster for adversarial pass) via `agenerate` with `temperature=0.0`. Appends invalid PMIDs to the findings list after the LLM response (line 116). Normalizes the verdict string to uppercase and validates it is in `{"PASS", "FAIL", "CONDITIONAL"}` (defaults to `"CONDITIONAL"` on invalid). Inserts `"direction_only_falsifier_v0"` at index 0 of `challenges_run` if not already present (per codex G10/G11 — honest scope labeling).

**External calls:**
- `Gemini 2.5 Flash` via Vertex AI — claim-direction match check.

### ADK Agent Declaration

**`auditor_adk`** (module-level `LlmAgent` instance, line 164)

```
LlmAgent(
    name="acp_auditor",
    model="gemini-2.5-flash",
    output_key="audit_verdict",
    instruction=AUDITOR_ADK_INSTRUCTION,
)
```

No tools — the auditor operates purely on the evidence JSON passed to it in context; does not need external tool calls. Instruction mirrors the runtime prompt logic but formatted for ADK context.

## Agent 7 — Report Writer / Cert Composer

**File:** `agents/report_writer.py`

**Pipeline stage:** Post-signing step, invoked by the API layer after `EndorsementClaimBundle` is signed. Not part of the orchestrator's `run_mesh` call. **Not on ADK** (locked Day-19 decision).

**Purpose:** Generates a brand-themed HTML verification certificate from the signed `EndorsementClaimBundle`. Enforces a strict honesty contract: required phrasing for each agent's output, forbidden phrases that would mislead buyers or regulators, and a locked verbatim disclosure block. The cert is injected into the demo dashboard's cert pane.

**Model:** `gemini-2.5-flash` (not Pro). The choice is deliberate: Flash returns in ~5–10s vs ~27s for Pro on cold instances, fitting inside the 40s cold-path budget. Extended thinking is explicitly disabled (`thinking_budget=0`) because HTML composition from structured data does not benefit from chain-of-thought.

### Honesty Contracts

Two module-level constants define the disclosure language that Gemini emits verbatim:

**`DISCLOSURE_BLOCK_INLINE`** (line 44): Single-line inline disclosure: `"Disclosure: AI-derived attestation · vet rubric is an LLM simulation · audit + Second Opinion are LLM agents over real evidence (PubMed, FTC §255, Google Search) · Ed25519 signed"`.

**`DISCLOSURE_BLOCK_FULL`** (line 51): HTML `<details>` expander with bullet-point scope disclosure. Lists: vet rubric = Gemini simulation, evidence = BioMCP real papers + Semantic Scholar, compliance = Vertex AI Search over public FTC corpus, auditor = PMID-format-only at v0.1, Second Opinion = Gemini + Google Search, signing = Ed25519 with mesh's own key (not 3rd-party accredited).

### Prompt

**`CERT_PROMPT`** (line 63)

Injected with `bundle_json` (trimmed bundle representation), `disclosure_inline`, and `disclosure_full_html`. The prompt is structured in five named sections:

**Required Phrasing table** maps each agent output to its mandated language:
- Vet rubric output → `"AI vet-rubric simulation"`, `"simulated 5-vet rubric"`, or `"AI-simulated vet rubric"`.
- Auditor output → `"Falsifier auditor"`, `"PMID-format check"`, `"claim-direction check"`.
- Citations → `"PubMed-retrieved papers"`, `"BioMCP-retrieved evidence"`.
- Compliance → `"FTC §255 substantiation check (Vertex AI Search grounded)"`.

**Forbidden Phrases** list: `"veterinary panel"`, `"vet panel"` (unless preceded by "simulated"), `"verified citations exist"`, `"licensed DVM"`, `"3rd-party accredited"`, `"FDA approved"`.

**Few-shot exemplars** for passing (vet 4/5, no FTC flag, audit PASS) and failing (vet 1/5, FTC flag, audit FAIL) claims show the correct narrative voice.

**Cert structure requirements:**
1. One-line headline: `"<brand> · <claim text> · <audit verdict>"`.
2. 150–200 word executive narrative readable by general counsel in 30 seconds.
3. `"Ship before launch"` section: 3 numbered actionable fixes.
4. Locked footer template with `bundle_urn`, `bundle_hash`, disclosure blocks.
5. Dark-mode CSS variable references (`--ink`, `--electric`, `--moss-glow`, `--signal`, `--warning`, `--muted`).

### Functions

**`_client() -> genai.Client`** (line 127): Returns Vertex AI Gemini client for `pawconscious-mesh-2026`.

**`compose_cert(bundle: EndorsementClaimBundle, bundle_hash: str | None, chain_anchor: str | None) -> str`** (async, line 131)

**Parameters:** `bundle`, `bundle_hash` (hex hash of signed bundle), `chain_anchor` (transparency log entry).  
**Returns:** Self-contained HTML fragment (no `<html>/<head>/<body>`).

Trims the bundle to only the fields the LLM needs (avoids wasting context on raw evidence dumps): `product_url`, `sku`, `bundle_urn`, `issued_at`, `claims` (text+kind only), `vet_scores` (score+rationale[:200]+escalate), `compliance` (ftc_section+violation_flag+rationale[:240]), `audit` (verdict+findings_count), `evidence_summary` (papers_count). Substitutes the two locked disclosure block constants into the prompt so Gemini emits them verbatim.

Post-processing on the response:
- Strips markdown fences (`` ``` `` or ` ```html `).
- Strips control characters except TAB and LF (prevents JSON parse failures on the wire).

**`_brand_from_url(url: str | None) -> str`** (line 209)

Derives a display brand label from the PDP URL hostname. Strips `www.` prefix, takes the first hostname segment, title-cases it. Returns `"This product"` on any failure.

**`static_cert(bundle: EndorsementClaimBundle, bundle_hash: str | None, chain_anchor: str | None) -> str`** (line 223)

Deterministic no-LLM fallback cert, built directly from bundle data via f-string interpolation. Invoked by the server when `compose_cert` times out or errors, ensuring a completed bundle always has a `cert_html` (a judge entering any URL must never see "No cert_html in response"). Uses the same locked disclosure blocks and forbidden-phrase-free phrasing. Uses `shared.verdict.compute_verdict` for the single-source verdict. HTML-escapes all user-supplied strings.

**External calls:**
- `Gemini 2.5 Flash` via Vertex AI — HTML certificate composition.

## Agent 8 — Second Opinion

**File:** `agents/second_opinion.py`

**Pipeline stage:** Post-signing step, invoked by the API layer after bundle signing and cert composition. Not part of `run_mesh`. **Not on ADK** (locked Day-19 decision).

**Purpose:** Adversarial double-validation. Takes the complete signed `EndorsementClaimBundle` and runs four stress-test probes using Google Search grounding (real-time web search) to find external evidence that could contradict the base mesh verification. Returns a structured verdict with per-test results and a strongest counter-argument.

**Architecture note:** The primary planned path is the Managed Agents API (Gemini 3.5 Flash with native web browsing). The file as shipped implements the fallback path: `gemini-2.5-pro` with `types.Tool(google_search=types.GoogleSearch())` grounding. The Managed Agents migration is queued behind a feature flag.

### Prompt

**`SECOND_OPINION_PROMPT`** (line 40)

Injected with `bundle_summary` (a compressed dict with brand/product, claim texts, vet scores, compliance violation flags, and audit verdicts). System role: adversarial double-validation layer running after five other agents.

Four stress tests, each with a `SURVIVES` / `NEEDS REVIEW` verdict:
1. **COURT** — would the claim survive a class-action plaintiff theory under FTC §255? Search for similar claims that resulted in settlements (prompt cites Cosequin $11.5M Nutramax 2024, Prevagen $165M as examples to search for).
2. **REGULATOR** — has the brand or claim type been subject to FTC enforcement, FDA warning letters, AAFCO action, or state AG inquiry?
3. **SCIENTIFIC CONSENSUS** — does peer-reviewed literature (last 24 months) contradict the claim mechanism?
4. **PUBLIC SKEPTICISM** — what does Reddit r/pets, ConsumerLab, science-blogger reviews, trade press say?

Returns strict JSON: `{"tests": [...], "strongest_counter": "...", "overall_verdict": "CONFIRMS" | "NEEDS REVIEW", "summary": "..."}`. Temperature is 0.3 (slight variation allowed for web-grounded reasoning; must reason about adversarial evidence). `max_output_tokens=4000`.

### Functions

**`_client() -> genai.Client`** (line 73): Returns Vertex AI Gemini client for `pawconscious-mesh-2026`.

**`get_second_opinion(bundle: EndorsementClaimBundle) -> dict`** (async, line 77)

**Parameters:** `bundle` — the signed bundle.  
**Returns:** Dict matching the prompt's JSON schema.

Compresses the bundle to a summary dict (brand/product, claim texts, vet scores with escalation flags, compliance violation flags, audit verdicts). Calls Gemini 2.5 Pro with `types.Tool(google_search=types.GoogleSearch())` — this activates real-time Google Search grounding.

Post-processing on the response (lines 107–124):
1. Strips markdown fences.
2. Strips Google Search citation markers like `[1]` or `[2][3]` that break JSON parsing.
3. Strips control characters except TAB and LF.
4. Extracts the outermost JSON object by finding the first `{` and last `}`.
5. Parses with `json.loads`.

**Failure mode:** On `JSONDecodeError`, returns a **fail-closed** response with `overall_verdict: "UNAVAILABLE"` (line 131). An adversarial agent must never silently agree on its own failure — `UNAVAILABLE` surfaces the gap in the UI rather than fabricating consensus.

**External calls:**
- `Gemini 2.5 Pro` via Vertex AI — reasoning.
- `Google Search` (via `types.GoogleSearch()` tool) — real-time web search for adversarial evidence.

## Agent 9 — COA Ingester

**File:** `agents/coa_ingester.py`

**Pipeline stage:** Separate from the main mesh pipeline. Invoked independently (e.g., via a form upload endpoint) when a brand provides a lab Certificate of Analysis PDF. Output attaches to the signed PCEC bundle under `attached_documents`. Not part of `run_mesh`.

**Purpose:** Multimodal evidence ingest. Takes raw PDF bytes of a brand's lab COA, runs Google Cloud Document AI OCR to extract text, then uses Gemini 2.5 Flash to parse the ingredient findings table. The resulting `COAExtraction` puts a real third-party lab document (not just LLM reasoning) in the bundle, hardening it against M&A diligence and plaintiff scrutiny.

**Document AI processor:**
- Type: `OCR_PROCESSOR` (Document OCR)
- Resource: `projects/40952019806/locations/us/processors/41c510c3067b6d6d`
- Region: `us`
- Cost: $1.50 per 1,000 pages (~$0.012 for an 8-page COA).

**v0.1 honest scope:** Extracts free text via OCR + Gemini field parsing. Does NOT validate against AOAC method codes, ISO 17025 lab accreditation, or batch chain-of-custody. v0.2 roadmap: Document AI Custom Extractor trained on labeled COAs.

### Data Models (Python dataclasses)

**`ExtractedFinding`** (dataclass, line 57)

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ingredient` | `str` | Ingredient name |
| `amount` | `str` | Measured amount |
| `unit` | `str` | Unit of measure |
| `raw_context` | `str` | Surrounding line from OCR for traceability |

**`COAExtraction`** (dataclass, line 68)

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `type` | `str` | `"coa"` / `"lab_report"` / `"dvm_letter"` |
| `source_pdf_sha256` | `str` | SHA-256 hex of the input PDF bytes |
| `source_pdf_bytes` | `int` | PDF size in bytes |
| `page_count` | `int` | Page count from Document AI response |
| `document_ai_processor` | `str` | Processor resource name |
| `raw_text` | `str` | Full OCR output |
| `findings` | `list[ExtractedFinding]` | Parsed ingredient tuples |
| `extracted_at` | `str` | ISO 8601 UTC timestamp |
| `note` | `str` | Honest disclaimer and optional label |

**`COAExtraction.to_bundle_dict() -> dict`** (line 81): Returns a JSON-safe dict shape for `PCECBundle.output.attached_documents[]`.

### Functions

**`_docai_client() -> documentai.DocumentProcessorServiceClient`** (line 95)

Returns a Document AI client pinned to `us-documentai.googleapis.com` (required because the processor lives in the `us` region, not `us-central1`).

**`_run_ocr(pdf_bytes: bytes, *, max_pages: int = 15) -> tuple[str, int]`** (line 104)

**Parameters:** `pdf_bytes`, `max_pages` (Document AI image mode caps at 15 pages per request; COA findings are typically in the first few pages).  
**Returns:** `(full_text, page_count)`.

Constructs a `documentai.RawDocument` with `mime_type="application/pdf"` and a `documentai.ProcessRequest` with `process_options.from_start=max_pages`. Calls `client.process_document`. Returns `document.text` and `len(document.pages)`. Raises on transport error; caller handles with `try/except`.

**`_gemini_parse_findings(ocr_text: str) -> list[ExtractedFinding]`** (line 133)

**Parameters:** `ocr_text` — up to 18,000 characters of OCR output.  
**Returns:** `list[ExtractedFinding]`.

Calls Gemini 2.5 Flash with `temperature=0.0` and `response_mime_type="application/json"`. Prompt instructs: find every ingredient with a measured amount and unit, skip testing methods/lab address/lot metadata, return a JSON array of `{ingredient, amount, unit, raw_context}`. If the OCR text is empty, returns an empty list without calling the LLM. On `JSONDecodeError`, returns empty list.

**Honest design note in docstring (line 136):** The LLM is used here because COA layout varies wildly across labs and a per-lab structured parser is not built yet.

**`ingest_coa(pdf_bytes: bytes, *, label: Optional[str] = None) -> COAExtraction`** (line 185)

**Parameters:** `pdf_bytes` — raw PDF content. `label` — optional friendly label for traceability.  
**Returns:** `COAExtraction`.

1. Computes SHA-256 of the PDF bytes.
2. Calls `_run_ocr(pdf_bytes)`. On any transport exception, returns a partial `COAExtraction` with `OCR_UNAVAILABLE: <exception>` in the `note` field (fail-open behavior so callers always get a result).
3. Calls `_gemini_parse_findings(raw_text)`.
4. Returns a complete `COAExtraction` with all fields populated.

**`main() -> None`** (line 230): CLI smoke test. Usage: `python agents/coa_ingester.py <pdf_path>`. Reads the PDF, calls `ingest_coa`, prints SHA256 prefix, page count, note, OCR length, extracted findings, and a truncated JSON payload preview.

**External calls:**
- `Google Cloud Document AI` (`documentai_v1.DocumentProcessorServiceClient`) — OCR.
- `Gemini 2.5 Flash` via Vertex AI — ingredient table parsing.

---

## Orchestrator

**File:** `agents/orchestrator.py`

**Purpose:** Wires all primary agents together into the full mesh pipeline. Manages the asyncio fan-out (equivalent to an ADK `ParallelAgent`), wraps each agent call in a telemetry span, assembles the `EndorsementClaimBundle`, and declares the ADK topology for `/health/mesh-shape` introspection.

**Pipeline topology (runtime):**

```
run_mesh(product_url)
  └─ extract_claims(url)                              [sequential, Step 1]
  └─ asyncio.gather(*[process_claim(c) for c in claims])  [parallel, Step 2]
       └─ per claim: process_claim(claim)
            ├─ grade_claim(claim)   → EvidenceBundle    [parallel branch 1]
            ├─ vet_score(claim)     → VetRubricScore     [parallel branch 2]
            └─ compliance_map(claim)→ ComplianceMapping  [parallel branch 3]
            └─ audit_bundle(evidence) → AuditVerdict     [sequential, Step 3]
  └─ assemble EndorsementClaimBundle                   [Step 4]
```

### Functions

**`_claim_id(claim: Claim) -> str`** (line 37)

Derives a 10-character SHA-1 hex prefix from the claim text. Used as the `claim_id` field in telemetry spans. The PCEC schema has no `id` field on `Claim`.

**`_grade_with_span(claim: Claim) -> EvidenceBundle`** (async, line 43)

Wraps `grade_claim` in an `agent_span("evidence-grader", claim_id=...)` context manager. On success emits a span with `outcome=ok` and `duration_ms`. On exception emits with `outcome=error` then re-raises.

**`_vet_with_span(claim: Claim) -> VetRubricScore`** (async, line 48)

Wraps `vet_score` (imported as `score_claim` from `agents.vet_rubric`) in `agent_span("vet-rubric", claim_id=...)`.

**`_compliance_with_span(claim: Claim) -> ComplianceMapping`** (async, line 53)

Wraps `compliance_map` in `agent_span("compliance", claim_id=...)`.

**`_audit_with_span(evidence: EvidenceBundle, claim_id: str) -> AuditVerdict`** (async, line 58)

Wraps `audit_bundle` in `agent_span("auditor", claim_id=...)`.

**`process_claim(claim: Claim) -> tuple[EvidenceBundle, VetRubricScore, ComplianceMapping, AuditVerdict]`** (async, line 63)

**Parameters:** `claim`.  
**Returns:** 4-tuple of the parallel + sequential results.

Runs the three parallel branches via `asyncio.gather`:
```python
evidence, vet, comp = await asyncio.gather(
    _grade_with_span(claim),
    _vet_with_span(claim),
    _compliance_with_span(claim),
)
```
Then runs the auditor sequentially on the evidence result:
```python
audit = await _audit_with_span(evidence, claim_id=_claim_id(claim))
```
Returns `(evidence, vet, comp, audit)`.

**`run_mesh(product_url: str, max_claims: int | None = None) -> EndorsementClaimBundle`** (async, line 77)

**Parameters:** `product_url` — PDP URL to analyze. `max_claims` — optional cap on claims (used for speed in verification).  
**Returns:** Assembled `EndorsementClaimBundle`.

Step 1: Claims `extract_claims(url)` inside an `agent_span("claim-extractor")`.  
Step 2: `asyncio.gather(*[process_claim(c) for c in claims])` — all claims processed in parallel.  
Step 3: Assembles `EndorsementClaimBundle` from the list of 4-tuples, aligning `evidence`, `vet_scores`, `compliance`, and `audit` lists by index with `claims`.  
Note: `sku` is set to the product URL in v0.1 (GTIN/ASIN extraction is a future step).

**`summarize(bundle: EndorsementClaimBundle) -> str`** (line 105)

**Parameters:** `bundle`.  
**Returns:** Plain-text summary for stdout or the Mesh Console UI.

Counts PASS/FAIL/CONDITIONAL audit verdicts, compliance violations (`violation_flag=True`), and vet escalations (`escalate_to_human_vet=True`). Prints per-claim detail: kind, claim text, paper count, vet score (with ESCALATE flag), FTC section and violation flag, audit verdict and finding count.

### ADK Topology Declaration

**`build_orchestrator_adk_topology() -> SequentialAgent`** (line 158)

Constructs (or returns the cached) ADK `SequentialAgent` representing the full mesh. Cached in `_ORCHESTRATOR_ADK_TOPOLOGY` because ADK enforces single-parent on agent instances — re-building would attempt to re-parent the `LlmAgent` singletons. The `claim_extractor_adk` is built once via `build_claim_extractor_agent()` and captured into the cached topology.

**Topology shape:**
```
acp_orchestrator (SequentialAgent)
  ├─ acp_claim_extractor   (LlmAgent + FunctionTool[fetch_pdp_html])
  ├─ acp_claim_fan_out     (ParallelAgent)
  │    ├─ acp_evidence_grader  (LlmAgent + FunctionTool[search_pubmed_for_adk])
  │    └─ acp_compliance       (LlmAgent + FunctionTool[retrieve_grounding_sources_for_adk])
  └─ acp_auditor           (LlmAgent, no tools)
```

**`describe_mesh_shape() -> dict`** (line 206)

Introspects the ADK topology recursively and returns a JSON-safe description for the `/health/mesh-shape` endpoint. For each agent node, captures: `name`, `type` (class name), `description`, `model`, `tools` (by name), `output_key`, and recursively `sub_agents`. Also includes:
- `agents_on_adk`: `["acp_claim_extractor", "acp_evidence_grader", "acp_compliance", "acp_auditor"]`
- `agents_off_adk_by_design`: `["vet_rubric", "report_writer", "second_opinion"]`
- `ratio_on_adk`: `"4/7"`
- `runtime_path`: `"asyncio.gather (shape-only; runtime parity preserved)"`
- Note explaining the ADK objects are real and introspectable; runtime uses asyncio fan-out for determinism.

**`_adk_version() -> str`** (line 257)

Returns `google.adk.__version__` or `"unknown"` if the import fails, ensuring the `/health/mesh-shape` endpoint never returns a 500.

**`main() -> None`** (line 269): Verification entrypoint. Runs `run_mesh` against `https://www.nativepet.com/products/hip-joint` with `max_claims=5` and prints `summarize(bundle)`.

---

| Agent Name (ADK) | File | ADK Type | Tools | Model | `output_key` | On ADK |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `acp_orchestrator` | `orchestrator.py` | `SequentialAgent` | — | — | — | Yes |
| `acp_claim_fan_out` | `orchestrator.py` | `ParallelAgent` | — | — | — | Yes (inner) |
| `acp_claim_extractor` | `claim_extractor.py` | `LlmAgent` | `fetch_pdp_html` (SSRF-guarded PDP fetch) | `gemini-2.5-pro` | — | Yes |
| `acp_evidence_grader` | `evidence_grader.py` | `LlmAgent` | `search_pubmed_for_adk` (BioMCP) | `gemini-2.5-pro` | `evidence_bundle` | Yes |
| `acp_compliance` | `compliance.py` | `LlmAgent` | `retrieve_grounding_sources_for_adk` (Vertex AI Search) | `gemini-2.5-pro` | `compliance_mapping` | Yes |
| `acp_auditor` | `auditor.py` | `LlmAgent` | None | `gemini-2.5-flash` | `audit_verdict` | Yes |
| `vet_rubric` | `vet_rubric.py` | direct genai | — | `gemini-2.5-pro` | — | No (by design) |
| `report_writer` | `report_writer.py` | direct genai | — | `gemini-2.5-flash` | — | No (by design) |
| `second_opinion` | `second_opinion.py` | direct genai | Google Search grounding | `gemini-2.5-pro` | — | No (by design) |
| `citation_enricher` | `citation_enricher.py` | HTTP only | Semantic Scholar API | — | — | No (not an LlmAgent) |
| `coa_ingester` | `coa_ingester.py` | Document AI + genai | Document AI OCR | `gemini-2.5-flash` | — | No (separate pipeline) |

**Runtime vs ADK:** The mesh runtime executes via `asyncio.gather` fan-out in `orchestrator.py:run_mesh`. The ADK objects (`SequentialAgent`, `ParallelAgent`, `LlmAgent` instances) are constructed and cached in module scope, exposed via `/health/mesh-shape` for structural verification, and represent the correct ADK topology shape. An ADK Runner runtime path behind a feature flag is planned for a future phase.

## Inter-Agent Wiring Diagram

```
product_url
    │
    ▼
[Agent 1] claim_extractor.extract_claims()
    │  → fetches PDP (httpx → SSRF guard → Firecrawl fallback)
    │  → Gemini 2.5 Pro: CLAIM_EXTRACTION_PROMPT
    │  → list[Claim]
    │
    ├─────────────────── asyncio.gather (one task per Claim) ──────────────────
    │
    │  Per claim: orchestrator.process_claim(claim)
    │  │
    │  ├─ [Agent 2] evidence_grader.grade_claim()          ─── parallel branch 1
    │  │    ├─ Gemini 2.5 Pro: KEYWORD_EXTRACTION_PROMPT
    │  │    ├─ BioMCP.search_articles() (via mcp or direct lib)
    │  │    ├─ Gemini 2.5 Pro: GRADING_PROMPT
    │  │    └─ [Agent 5] citation_enricher.enrich_with_citations()
    │  │         └─ Semantic Scholar batch API
    │  │    → EvidenceBundle
    │  │
    │  ├─ [Agent 3] vet_rubric.score_claim()               ─── parallel branch 2
    │  │    └─ Gemini 2.5 Pro: VET_RUBRIC_PROMPT
    │  │    → VetRubricScore
    │  │
    │  └─ [Agent 4] compliance.map_claim()                 ─── parallel branch 3
    │       ├─ Vertex AI Search: regulatory corpus retrieval
    │       └─ Gemini 2.5 Pro: COMPLIANCE_PROMPT + grounding block
    │       → ComplianceMapping
    │
    │  [Agent 6] auditor.audit_bundle(evidence)            ─── sequential step
    │       ├─ PMID_REGEX pre-flight (no LLM)
    │       └─ Gemini 2.5 Flash: AUDIT_PROMPT
    │       → AuditVerdict
    │
    │──────────────────── gather results ──────────────────────────────────────
    │
    ▼
orchestrator.run_mesh() assembles EndorsementClaimBundle
    │
    ▼  (downstream, API layer, post-signing)
[Agent 7] report_writer.compose_cert()
    └─ Gemini 2.5 Flash (thinking_budget=0): CERT_PROMPT
    → HTML cert fragment

[Agent 8] second_opinion.get_second_opinion()
    └─ Gemini 2.5 Pro + Google Search grounding: SECOND_OPINION_PROMPT
    → dict {tests, strongest_counter, overall_verdict, summary}

[Agent 9] coa_ingester.ingest_coa()   (separate upload path)
    ├─ Document AI OCR Processor
    └─ Gemini 2.5 Flash: ingredient parse prompt
    → COAExtraction → bundle.attached_documents[]
```

## 1. Module Overview

`services/mesh_api/main.py` is the single FastAPI application that constitutes the public-facing surface of the PawConscious Mesh. It is 2094 lines long. The file contains:

- The FastAPI `app` instance with all route definitions.
- Module-level in-process state: the idempotency cache, the DoS concurrency guard, the Agent Engine traffic gate and latency windows.
- The A2A v0.3 task lifecycle: `POST /a2a/v1/tasks/send` (202 Accepted, fire-and-forget background worker), `GET /a2a/v1/tasks/get/{task_id}` (polling), `POST /a2a/v1/tasks/cancel/{task_id}`.
- The PCEC v0.1 resolver at `/pcec/v0/claim/{urn}`.
- The hot-path lookup at `GET /a2a/v1/lookup`.
- Chain head at `GET /pcec/v0/chain/head`.
- The signed report renderer at `GET /report/{urn}`.
- The Gemini-grounded public chat surface at `POST /api/ask-gemini`.
- Five HTML page routes (`/`, `/demo`, `/agents`, `/architecture`, `/founder`) each served from static HTML files with server-side chrome injection.
- Five health/introspection routes.
- Agent card and DID document at `/.well-known/`.
- Bundle hashing (`compute_bundle_hash`) and Ed25519 signing (`sign_bundle`, `_load_signer`).
- Global nav, footer, and CSS chrome as Python string constants (`_GLOBAL_CHROME_CSS`, `_GLOBAL_NAV_TEMPLATE`, `_GLOBAL_FOOTER_HTML`).

The module-level docstring (lines 1–16) describes this as the public A2A v0.3 endpoint with demo API-key gating active during the hackathon period. The API key gate is explicitly described as temporary; public open access ships post-hackathon.

## 3. Environment Variables

All environment variables read by this module, their defaults, and their effects:

| Variable | Default | Type | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ACP_MAX_CONCURRENT_VERIFIES` | `"3"` | int | Maximum number of concurrent in-flight `run_mesh` calls per Cloud Run instance. Requests exceeding this limit receive HTTP 429. Paired with `--max-instances=4` in `cloudbuild.yaml` for a hard fleet ceiling of 12. |
| `ACP_DEMO_API_KEY` | `"demo-key-2026-06"` | str | The API key checked against `X-API-Key` header on `POST /a2a/v1/tasks/send`. |
| `ACP_PUBLIC_BASE_URL` | `"https://mesh-api-40952019806.us-central1.run.app"` | str | Canonical base URL for self-referencing poll URLs, agent card, DID document service endpoints, and the `<!--PUBLIC_BASE_URL-->` marker substitution in static HTML. |
| `ACP_PUBLIC_DID` | `"did:web:<host>"` (derived from `ACP_PUBLIC_BASE_URL`) | str | The DID identifier used in the DID document and in Ed25519 signature strings. |
| `ACP_DEFAULT_MAX_CLAIMS` | `"3"` | int | Default number of claims to extract and verify per product URL when `max_claims` is not specified in the request. |
| `ACP_AGENT_ENGINE_RESOURCE` | `"projects/40952019806/locations/us-central1/reasoningEngines/1255381144908595200"` | str | Fully-qualified Vertex AI Reasoning Engine resource name. Parsed to extract project number and location for `vertexai.init()`. |
| `ACP_USE_AGENT_ENGINE` | `"false"` | bool | Feature flag. When `"true"`, `_traffic_gate_open` starts as `True` and new `verify_claim` tasks are routed to the Reasoning Engine (subject to the p95 auto-fallback gate). |
| `ACP_AGENT_ENGINE_P95_GATE` | `"2.0"` | float | The gate multiplier. If Agent Engine p95 latency exceeds this multiple of inline p95, the traffic gate closes automatically. |
| `ACP_AGENT_ENGINE_MIN_SAMPLES` | `"5"` | int | Minimum number of latency samples in each window before the p95 gate comparison is evaluated. |
| `ACP_LATENCY_WINDOW_SIZE` | `"20"` | int | Rolling window size (number of most recent samples) for both inline and Agent Engine latency deques. |
| `ACP_INLINE_P95_BASELINE_MS` | `"90000"` | float | Fallback inline p95 (in milliseconds) used for the gate comparison when not enough live inline samples exist. Default 90000ms = 90s matches observed inline p95 from L1 evaluation. |
| `ACP_AGENT_ENGINE_QUERY_TIMEOUT_S` | `"180"` | float | Hard per-request timeout for `engine.query()` calls. On `asyncio.TimeoutError`, the call is treated as a failure: latency is recorded as the timeout value, the inline fallback fires, and the consecutive-failure counter increments. |
| `ACP_SIGNING_KEY_PEM_PATH` | _(none)_ | str | Path to a local PEM file for the Ed25519 private key. Used in dev; takes precedence over Secret Manager. Never committed (covered by `.gitignore`). |
| `PORT` | `"8080"` | int | Port for the `uvicorn.run()` call at `__main__`. |
