```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# v6 submission video mix · 2:00 cap · SOUL-FIRST.
#
# Bookended by Veo Trufa shots (opening + closing). Lyria with emotional
# arc (warm → tension → quiet → relief → swell → warm resolution).
# Real screen capture for the product story. Antoni warmer + slower.
#
# Beats:
#   1  0:00-0:10  Veo opening Trufa (8s) + scene-0 start (2s)
#   2  0:10-0:20  passA[0-10] real Gemini cold open
#   3  0:20-0:35  title card 6s + scene-2b begin 9s
#   4  0:35-1:00  passA[18-43] scene-2b BLOCK + replacement copy
#   5  1:00-1:15  passB[0-15] scene-2 PASS + chain anchor
#   6  1:15-1:30  passD[0-15] /agents page slow scroll
#   7  1:30-1:45  passC[0-15] /architecture SVG pan
#   8  1:45-2:00  Veo closing Trufa (8s) + end card fade-in (7s)

set -euo pipefail

DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
RAW_V4="$DIR/raw-v4"
RAW_V5="$DIR/raw-v5"
VEO_V6="$DIR/veo-v6"
VO="$DIR/vo-v6"
MUSIC="$DIR/music-v3"
OUT="$DIR/pawconscious-demo-v6-soul.mp4"
WORK="$DIR/_work_v6"

mkdir -p "$WORK"

# Sanity
for f in "$RAW_V4/passA.webm" "$RAW_V4/passB.webm" "$RAW_V4/passC.webm" "$RAW_V4/passD.webm" \
         "$RAW_V5/title_beat3.png" "$RAW_V5/end_card_v5.png" \
         "$VEO_V6/opening_trufa.mp4" "$VEO_V6/closing_trufa_verified.mp4" \
         "$MUSIC/bed.wav"; do
  [ -f "$f" ] || { echo "missing $f" >&2; exit 1; }
done
for n in 01 02 03 04 05 06 07 08; do
  [ -f "$VO/beat-$n.mp3" ] || { echo "missing beat-$n.mp3" >&2; exit 1; }
done

W=1920
H=1080
FPS=30
BG="#0E1218"

echo "[v6 mix] building visual segments..."

# Beat 1 — Veo opening Trufa (8s) + 2s of scene-0 hint
ffmpeg -y -i "$VEO_V6/opening_trufa.mp4" -t 8 -an \
  -c:v libx264 -preset slow -crf 18 -r $FPS \
  -vf "scale=$W:$H:force_original_aspect_ratio=decrease,pad=$W:$H:(ow-iw)/2:(oh-ih)/2:color=$BG,format=yuv420p" \
  "$WORK/b1a_veo.mp4" 2>&1 | tail -1
ffmpeg -y -i "$RAW_V4/passA.webm" -t 2 -an \
  -c:v libx264 -preset slow -crf 18 -r $FPS \
  -vf "scale=$W:$H,format=yuv420p" \
  "$WORK/b1b_demo.mp4" 2>&1 | tail -1

# Beat 2 — passA[0-10] real Gemini cold open
# (We already used 0-2s in beat 1 tail; this is 2-12s of passA.)
ffmpeg -y -ss 2 -i "$RAW_V4/passA.webm" -t 10 -an \
  -c:v libx264 -preset slow -crf 18 -r $FPS \
  -vf "scale=$W:$H,format=yuv420p" \
  "$WORK/b2.mp4" 2>&1 | tail -1

# Beat 3 — title card 6s + scene-2b begin 9s
ffmpeg -y -loop 1 -i "$RAW_V5/title_beat3.png" -t 6 -pix_fmt yuv420p \
  -c:v libx264 -preset slow -crf 18 -r $FPS -vf "scale=$W:$H" \
  "$WORK/b3a_title.mp4" 2>&1 | tail -1
ffmpeg -y -ss 14 -i "$RAW_V4/passA.webm" -t 9 -an \
  -c:v libx264 -preset slow -crf 18 -r $FPS \
  -vf "scale=$W:$H,format=yuv420p" \

# Beat 4 — passA[23-48] scene-2b BLOCK fills + replacement copy (25s)
ffmpeg -y -ss 23 -i "$RAW_V4/passA.webm" -t 25 -an \
  -c:v libx264 -preset slow -crf 18 -r $FPS \
  -vf "scale=$W:$H,format=yuv420p" \
  "$WORK/b4.mp4" 2>&1 | tail -1

# Beat 5 — passB[0-15] scene-2 PASS + chain anchor (15s)
ffmpeg -y -i "$RAW_V4/passB.webm" -t 15 -an \
  -c:v libx264 -preset slow -crf 18 -r $FPS \
  -vf "scale=$W:$H,format=yuv420p" \
  "$WORK/b5.mp4" 2>&1 | tail -1

# Beat 6 — passD[0-15] /agents page (15s)
ffmpeg -y -i "$RAW_V4/passD.webm" -t 15 -an \
  -c:v libx264 -preset slow -crf 18 -r $FPS \
  -vf "scale=$W:$H,format=yuv420p" \
  "$WORK/b6.mp4" 2>&1 | tail -1

# Beat 7 — passC[0-15] /architecture (15s)
ffmpeg -y -i "$RAW_V4/passC.webm" -t 15 -an \
  -c:v libx264 -preset slow -crf 18 -r $FPS \
  -vf "scale=$W:$H,format=yuv420p" \
  "$WORK/b7.mp4" 2>&1 | tail -1

# Beat 8 — Veo closing (8s) + end card (7s with crossfade fade-in)
ffmpeg -y -i "$VEO_V6/closing_trufa_verified.mp4" -t 8 -an \
  -c:v libx264 -preset slow -crf 18 -r $FPS \
  -vf "scale=$W:$H:force_original_aspect_ratio=decrease,pad=$W:$H:(ow-iw)/2:(oh-ih)/2:color=$BG,fade=t=out:st=7:d=1:color=$BG,format=yuv420p" \
  "$WORK/b8a_closing.mp4" 2>&1 | tail -1
ffmpeg -y -loop 1 -i "$RAW_V5/end_card_v5.png" -t 7 -pix_fmt yuv420p \
  -c:v libx264 -preset slow -crf 18 -r $FPS \
  -vf "scale=$W:$H,fade=t=in:st=0:d=1:color=$BG,fade=t=out:st=5:d=2:color=$BG" \
  "$WORK/b8b_end.mp4" 2>&1 | tail -1

# Concat
cat > "$WORK/concat.txt" <<EOF
file '$WORK/b1a_veo.mp4'
file '$WORK/b1b_demo.mp4'
file '$WORK/b2.mp4'
file '$WORK/b3a_title.mp4'
file '$WORK/b3b_block_start.mp4'
file '$WORK/b4.mp4'
file '$WORK/b5.mp4'
file '$WORK/b6.mp4'
file '$WORK/b7.mp4'
file '$WORK/b8a_closing.mp4'
file '$WORK/b8b_end.mp4'
EOF
ffmpeg -y -f concat -safe 0 -i "$WORK/concat.txt" -c copy "$WORK/visual.mp4" 2>&1 | tail -1
VISUAL_DUR=$(ffprobe -v error -show_entries format=duration -of default=noprint_wrappers=1:nokey=1 "$WORK/visual.mp4")
echo "[v6 mix] visual: ${VISUAL_DUR}s"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# VO chain. Beat starts in ms (matches storyboard exactly):
#   b1 @ 0      b2 @ 10000  b3 @ 20000  b4 @ 35000
#   b5 @ 60000  b6 @ 75000  b7 @ 90000  b8 @ 105000
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
declare -a STARTS=(0 10000 20000 35000 60000 75000 90000 105000)
declare -a BEATS=(01 02 03 04 05 06 07 08)

INPUTS=""
FILTER=""
for i in "${!BEATS[@]}"; do
  b=${BEATS[$i]}
  ms=${STARTS[$i]}
  INPUTS="$INPUTS -i $VO/beat-$b.mp3"
  FILTER="$FILTER[$i:a]adelay=${ms}|${ms}[a$i];"
done
MIXES=""
for i in "${!BEATS[@]}"; do MIXES="$MIXES[a$i]"; done
FILTER="${FILTER}${MIXES}amix=inputs=${#BEATS[@]}:duration=longest:normalize=0,apad=whole_dur=120,atrim=0:120,asetpts=PTS-STARTPTS"
ffmpeg -y $INPUTS -filter_complex "$FILTER" -c:a aac -b:a 192k -ar 44100 -ac 2 "$WORK/vo.m4a" 2>&1 | tail -1

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Music bed with EMOTIONAL ARC. Volume envelope:
#   0-10s   warm intro (0.60) - Trufa opening
#   10-20s  steady (0.55)     - Gemini ships
#   20-35s  tension build (0.55→0.45) - title + block start
#   35-58s  block tension (0.45→0.30) - bento fills + verdict
#   58-60s  near-silent (0.10) - the protected frame moment
#   60-75s  relief warmth (0.50) - PASS + chain anchor
#   75-90s  steady (0.55)     - developer surface
#   90-105s building swell (0.60) - architecture
#   105-117s peak warm resolution (0.65) - closing Veo
#   117-120s fade to silence (0.65→0)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
ffmpeg -y -i "$MUSIC/bed.wav" -filter_complex "
  [0:a]
  atrim=0:120,
  asetpts=PTS-STARTPTS,
  volume='
    if(lt(t,10), 0.60,
    if(lt(t,20), 0.55,
    if(lt(t,35), 0.55 - (t-20)/15 * 0.10,
    if(lt(t,58), 0.45 - (t-35)/23 * 0.15,
    if(lt(t,60), 0.10,
    if(lt(t,75), 0.50,
    if(lt(t,90), 0.55,
    if(lt(t,105), 0.55 + (t-90)/15 * 0.10,
    if(lt(t,117), 0.65,
    if(lt(t,120), 0.65 * (1 - (t-117)/3),
    0))))))))))':eval=frame
  [out]
" -map "[out]" -c:a aac -b:a 160k -ar 44100 -ac 2 "$WORK/music_arc.m4a" 2>&1 | tail -1
echo "[v6 mix] music arc built"

# Mix VO + music with sidechain (gentle ratio 4 so the arc still breathes)
ffmpeg -y -i "$WORK/vo.m4a" -i "$WORK/music_arc.m4a" -filter_complex "
  [1:a][0:a]sidechaincompress=threshold=0.05:ratio=4:attack=20:release=400:makeup=1[ducked];
  [0:a][ducked]amix=inputs=2:duration=longest:normalize=0,
  alimiter=limit=0.95
" -c:a aac -b:a 192k -ar 44100 -ac 2 "$WORK/audio.m4a" 2>&1 | tail -1
echo "[v6 mix] audio built (arc + sidechain)"

# Final mux
ffmpeg -y -i "$WORK/visual.mp4" -i "$WORK/audio.m4a" \
  -map 0:v -map 1:a -c:v copy -c:a copy -movflags +faststart \
  -t 120 "$OUT" 2>&1 | tail -1

echo
echo "FINAL: $OUT"
ffprobe -v error -show_entries format=duration,bit_rate -show_entries stream=codec_name,width,height -of default=noprint_wrappers=1 "$OUT"
echo "Size: $(du -h "$OUT" | cut -f1)"
```

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# v6.1 mix — soul + Corcho + chews + no overlap + product on phone.
#
# Changes from v6:
# - VO regenerated with Corcho/10yo/no Mesh/improved pricing/tightened beat 7
# - Veo opening regen with chews jar (not liquid tincture)
# - Veo closing regen with phone product card visible
# - Beat 7 VO now 12s instead of 17s — fixes the 1:46 overlap
#
# Output: pawconscious-demo-v6.1-soul-corcho.mp4

done

W=1920; H=1080; FPS=30; BG="#0E1218"

# b1b — 2s scene-0 start

  -c:v libx264 -preset slow -crf 18 -r $FPS -vf "scale=$W:$H,format=yuv420p" \
  "$WORK/b2.mp4" 2>&1 | tail -1
# b3a — title card (6s)
ffmpeg -y -loop 1 -i "$RAW_V5/title_beat3.png" -t 6 -pix_fmt yuv420p \
  -c:v libx264 -preset slow -crf 18 -r $FPS -vf "scale=$W:$H" \

# b3b — scene-2b begin (9s)
ffmpeg -y -ss 14 -i "$RAW_V4/passA.webm" -t 9 -an \

# b5 — passB[0-15] PASS (15s)
ffmpeg -y -i "$RAW_V4/passB.webm" -t 15 -an \
  -c:v libx264 -preset slow -crf 18 -r $FPS -vf "scale=$W:$H,format=yuv420p" \
  "$WORK/b5.mp4" 2>&1 | tail -1
# b6 — passD[0-15] /agents (15s)
ffmpeg -y -i "$RAW_V4/passD.webm" -t 15 -an \
  -c:v libx264 -preset slow -crf 18 -r $FPS -vf "scale=$W:$H,format=yuv420p" \
  "$WORK/b6.mp4" 2>&1 | tail -1
# b7 — passC[0-15] /architecture (15s)
ffmpeg -y -i "$RAW_V4/passC.webm" -t 15 -an \

  "$WORK/b7.mp4" 2>&1 | tail -1
# b8a — Veo closing Corcho + product on phone (8s) with fade-out tail
ffmpeg -y -i "$VEO/closing_corcho_product.mp4" -t 8 -an \
  -c:v libx264 -preset slow -crf 18 -r $FPS \
  -vf "scale=$W:$H:force_original_aspect_ratio=decrease,pad=$W:$H:(ow-iw)/2:(oh-ih)/2:color=$BG,fade=t=out:st=7:d=1:color=$BG,format=yuv420p" \
  "$WORK/b8a_closing.mp4" 2>&1 | tail -1
# b8b — end card (7s) with fade-in + fade-out tail

  "$WORK/b8b_end.mp4" 2>&1 | tail -1

# Concat
cat > "$WORK/concat.txt" <<EOF
file '$WORK/b1a_veo.mp4'
file '$WORK/b1b_demo.mp4'
file '$WORK/b2.mp4'
file '$WORK/b3a_title.mp4'
file '$WORK/b3b_block_start.mp4'
file '$WORK/b4.mp4'
file '$WORK/b5.mp4'
file '$WORK/b6.mp4'
file '$WORK/b7.mp4'
file '$WORK/b8a_closing.mp4'
file '$WORK/b8b_end.mp4'
EOF
ffmpeg -y -f concat -safe 0 -i "$WORK/concat.txt" -c copy "$WORK/visual.mp4" 2>&1 | tail -1
VISUAL_DUR=$(ffprobe -v error -show_entries format=duration -of default=noprint_wrappers=1:nokey=1 "$WORK/visual.mp4")
echo "[v6.1 mix] visual: ${VISUAL_DUR}s"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# VO chain (unchanged beat starts; beat 7 VO is just shorter now so no overlap)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
declare -a STARTS=(0 10000 20000 35000 60000 75000 90000 105000)
declare -a BEATS=(01 02 03 04 05 06 07 08)
INPUTS=""
FILTER=""
for i in "${!BEATS[@]}"; do
  b=${BEATS[$i]}
  ms=${STARTS[$i]}
  INPUTS="$INPUTS -i $VO/beat-$b.mp3"
  FILTER="$FILTER[$i:a]adelay=${ms}|${ms}[a$i];"
done
MIXES=""
for i in "${!BEATS[@]}"; do MIXES="$MIXES[a$i]"; done
FILTER="${FILTER}${MIXES}amix=inputs=${#BEATS[@]}:duration=longest:normalize=0,apad=whole_dur=120,atrim=0:120,asetpts=PTS-STARTPTS"
ffmpeg -y $INPUTS -filter_complex "$FILTER" -c:a aac -b:a 192k -ar 44100 -ac 2 "$WORK/vo.m4a" 2>&1 | tail -1

# Music arc (unchanged from v6)
ffmpeg -y -i "$MUSIC/bed.wav" -filter_complex "
  [0:a]
  atrim=0:120,
  asetpts=PTS-STARTPTS,
  volume='
    if(lt(t,10), 0.60,
    if(lt(t,20), 0.55,
    if(lt(t,35), 0.55 - (t-20)/15 * 0.10,
    if(lt(t,58), 0.45 - (t-35)/23 * 0.15,
    if(lt(t,60), 0.10,
    if(lt(t,75), 0.50,
    if(lt(t,90), 0.55,
    if(lt(t,105), 0.55 + (t-90)/15 * 0.10,
    if(lt(t,117), 0.65,
    if(lt(t,120), 0.65 * (1 - (t-117)/3),
    0))))))))))':eval=frame
  [out]
" -map "[out]" -c:a aac -b:a 160k -ar 44100 -ac 2 "$WORK/music_arc.m4a" 2>&1 | tail -1

# Mix VO + music
ffmpeg -y -i "$WORK/vo.m4a" -i "$WORK/music_arc.m4a" -filter_complex "
  [1:a][0:a]sidechaincompress=threshold=0.05:ratio=4:attack=20:release=400:makeup=1[ducked];
  [0:a][ducked]amix=inputs=2:duration=longest:normalize=0,
  alimiter=limit=0.95
" -c:a aac -b:a 192k -ar 44100 -ac 2 "$WORK/audio.m4a" 2>&1 | tail -1

# Final
ffmpeg -y -i "$WORK/visual.mp4" -i "$WORK/audio.m4a" \
  -map 0:v -map 1:a -c:v copy -c:a copy -movflags +faststart \
  -t 120 "$OUT" 2>&1 | tail -1

echo
echo "FINAL: $OUT"
ffprobe -v error -show_entries format=duration,bit_rate -show_entries stream=codec_name,width,height -of default=noprint_wrappers=1 "$OUT"
echo "Size: $(du -h "$OUT" | cut -f1)"
```

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Headless Chromium screen recording of the PawConscious demo at
http://localhost:8088/demo. Drives the 5 scenes via JS evaluate at
pre-computed timestamps so the visuals sync to the 6 narration beats.

Outputs: demo/captures/recording.webm (silent 1920x1080)
Mixed into final MP4 by mix_video.sh.
"""
import asyncio
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path
from playwright.async_api import async_playwright

OUT_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "raw"
OUT_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

# Wall-clock milestones (seconds from t=0). Tuned so each beat's spoken duration
# lands inside the matching visual span.
#
#   visual span                                  VO beat playing
#   0.0 - 1.0   intro hold                       (silent)
#   1.0 - 5.0   scene 0 desktop -> chrome -> URL beat 1 (4.37s) "AI shopping...confident..."
#   5.0 - 9.0   gemini loads -> hello -> query   beat 2 (3.81s) "pet owner asks Gemini..."
#   9.0 - 13.0  query submit -> dive -> scene 1  beat 3 (3.85s) "finds three options...routes..."
#  13.0 - 19.5  scene 2 bento lights up + VERIFIED   beat 4 (5.80s) HERO "trust layer. evidence..."
#  19.5 - 24.0  scene 3 recommendation -> open product  beat 5 (3.67s) "one pick comes back..."
#  24.0 - 30.0  scene 4 vendor -> checkout -> receipt   beat 6 (5.20s) "trusted because verified"
#  30.0 - 32.0  hold receipt frame                (silent tail)

VIDEO_W, VIDEO_H = 1920, 1080

async def main() -> int:
    async with async_playwright() as pw:
        browser = await pw.chromium.launch(headless=True)
        ctx = await browser.new_context(
            viewport={"width": VIDEO_W, "height": VIDEO_H},
            record_video_dir=str(OUT_DIR),
            record_video_size={"width": VIDEO_W, "height": VIDEO_H},
            device_scale_factor=1.0,
        )
        # Inject CSS that hides the demo harness BEFORE the page paints,
        # so the controls bar + keyboard hint never appear in any frame.
        await ctx.add_init_script("""
          window.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', () => {
            const s = document.createElement('style');
            s.textContent = '.controls{display:none!important}.kbd-hint{display:none!important}.skip-intro{display:none!important}.replay-scene{display:none!important}';
            document.head.appendChild(s);
          });
        """)
        page = await ctx.new_page()
        print("[rec] navigating to /demo ...")
        await page.goto("http://localhost:8088/demo", wait_until="networkidle")
        # Boot lag.
        await asyncio.sleep(0.4)

        # Pause autoplay; we drive scenes manually for exact sync.
        await page.evaluate("if (window.runToken !== undefined) runToken += 1;")
        await asyncio.sleep(0.5)
        # Trigger scene 0 fresh.
        await page.evaluate("playScene(0)")

        print("[rec] t=00.0 scene 0 (desktop + chrome + URL + gemini + query)")
        # Let scene 0 fully play: native runScene0 takes ~8.5s end-to-end.
        await asyncio.sleep(9.0)

        # T=9.0  click submit → dive into scene 1.
        print("[rec] t=09.0 click submit (zoom into Gemini answer)")
        await page.evaluate("document.getElementById('s0-submit').click()")
        await asyncio.sleep(3.8)  # scene 1 products fade in + ping

        # T=12.8 click verify-with-PawConscious
        print("[rec] t=12.8 click verify-with-PawConscious")
        await page.evaluate("document.getElementById('goToPawConscious').click()")
        # Scene 2 cards × 5 × 520ms = 2.6s + verified moment + trust report
        await asyncio.sleep(6.6)

        # T=19.4 click see-Gemini-answer
        print("[rec] t=19.4 click see Gemini's answer")
        await page.evaluate("document.getElementById('goToRecommend').click()")
        await asyncio.sleep(3.4)  # tightened to give scene 4 more room

        # T=22.8 click open-verified-product
        print("[rec] t=22.8 click open verified product")
        await page.evaluate("document.getElementById('goToVendor').click()")
        # Scene 4 autonomous: ~5.4s end-to-end (cursor + add to cart + cursor + pay + processing)
        # Confirmation lands around T=28.2s, plays during beat 6 (24.5-29.7s).
        await asyncio.sleep(5.6)

        # Hold the confirmation frame.
        print("[rec] t=28.4 hold confirmation")
        await asyncio.sleep(3.0)

        # Wrap.
        await ctx.close()
        await browser.close()

        # Playwright writes the video on context close. Rename for clarity.
        videos = sorted(OUT_DIR.glob("*.webm"))
        if not videos:
            print("[rec] ERROR: no .webm produced", file=sys.stderr)
            return 1
        latest = videos[-1]
        final = OUT_DIR / "recording.webm"
        if latest != final:
            if final.exists():
                final.unlink()
            latest.rename(final)
        print(f"[rec] ok -> {final}")
        # Total wall-clock from t=0 to here was ~32.8s; playwright video should
        # match that closely.
        return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(asyncio.run(main()))
```

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""V2 screen recording. Slower scene pacing so each beat lands cleanly.

Timeline (40s, inserted between 2s intro card and 3s end card = 45s total):
  T=00.0 - 07.5  scene 0: macOS desktop -> chrome -> URL (beat 1 + 2 narrate)
  T=07.5 - 11.5  scene 0 finishes: gemini loads, query types
  T=11.5         submit click -> dive into scene 1
  T=11.5 - 15.5  scene 1 products fade in (beat 3 narrates)
  T=15.5         click verify-with-PawConscious
  T=15.5 - 28.5  scene 2 bento lights up sequentially + VERIFIED + Trust Report
                 (beat 4 HERO crescendo, 13s window matches the 13s VO beat)
  T=28.5         click see-Gemini's-answer
  T=28.5 - 31.5  scene 3 recommendation (beat 5 narrates)
  T=31.5         click open verified product
  T=31.5 - 39.5  scene 4 vendor + checkout + receipt (beat 6 narrates)
  T=39.5 - 40    hold receipt
"""
import asyncio
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from playwright.async_api import async_playwright

OUT_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "raw-v2"
OUT_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

VIDEO_W, VIDEO_H = 1920, 1080

            record_video_size={"width": VIDEO_W, "height": VIDEO_H},
            device_scale_factor=1.0,
        )
        # Hide harness chrome before any frame paints.
        await ctx.add_init_script("""
          window.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', () => {
            const s = document.createElement('style');
            s.textContent = '.controls{display:none!important}.kbd-hint{display:none!important}.skip-intro{display:none!important}.replay-scene{display:none!important}';
            document.head.appendChild(s);
          });
        """)
        page = await ctx.new_page()
        print("[rec-v2] navigating to /demo ...")
        await page.goto("http://localhost:8088/demo", wait_until="networkidle")
        await asyncio.sleep(0.4)

        await page.evaluate("if (window.runToken !== undefined) runToken += 1;")
        await asyncio.sleep(0.5)
        await page.evaluate("playScene(0)")

        # Scene 0 plays for ~10s natively (cursor + chrome + URL + gemini + query).
        print("[rec-v2] T=0.0 scene 0")
        await asyncio.sleep(11.0)

        # Click submit -> dive into scene 1.
        print("[rec-v2] T=11.0 click submit")
        await page.evaluate("document.getElementById('s0-submit').click()")
        # Scene 1 native: 500ms wait + 800ms show-products + then pinging.

        print("[rec-v2] T=15.5 click verify-with-PawConscious")
        await page.evaluate("document.getElementById('goToPawConscious').click()")
        # Scene 2 native: cards × 5 × 520ms = 2.6s + 180ms + complete pulse.
        # Hold 13s window for beat 4 hero to land.
        await asyncio.sleep(13.0)

        print("[rec-v2] T=28.5 click see-Gemini's-answer")
        await page.evaluate("document.getElementById('goToRecommend').click()")
        await asyncio.sleep(3.0)

        print("[rec-v2] T=31.5 click open verified product")
        await page.evaluate("document.getElementById('goToVendor').click()")
        # Scene 4 autonomous ~5.4s + 1s hold before receipt is stable.
        await asyncio.sleep(7.5)

        # Hold the receipt frame to fully settle.
        print("[rec-v2] T=39.0 hold confirmation")
        await asyncio.sleep(1.5)

        await ctx.close()
        await browser.close()

        videos = sorted(OUT_DIR.glob("*.webm"))
        if not videos:
            print("[rec-v2] ERROR: no .webm produced", file=sys.stderr)
            return 1
        latest = videos[-1]
        final = OUT_DIR / "recording.webm"
        if latest != final:
            if final.exists():
                final.unlink()
            latest.rename(final)
        print(f"[rec-v2] ok -> {final}")
        return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
```

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""V3 submission video screen captures (3 passes + 3 title cards).

Pass A (intro=block + judge=1): scene-0 → scene-1 (the "would have shipped"
  cold open) → scene-2b BLOCK. Covers beats 1, 2, 4, 5.
Pass B (default + judge=1): scene-2 PASS (hip-joint) → scene-3
  recommendation → scene-4 vendor + checkout. Covers beats 6, 7, 8.
Pass C: /architecture page slow vertical pan. Covers beat 9.

Title cards (beats 3, 10, end): rendered as 1080p PNGs from the HTML
files in demo/captures/cards/.

Output:
  demo/captures/raw-v3/passA.webm      ~32s
  demo/captures/raw-v3/passB.webm      ~46s
  demo/captures/raw-v3/passC.webm      ~14s
  demo/captures/raw-v3/title_beat3.png
  demo/captures/raw-v3/title_beat10.png
  demo/captures/raw-v3/end_card.png
"""
import asyncio
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from playwright.async_api import async_playwright

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
OUT = ROOT / "raw-v3"
OUT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
CARDS = ROOT / "cards"

W, H = 1920, 1080
BASE = "http://localhost:8088"

HIDE_CHROME_CSS = """
.controls { display: none !important; }
.kbd-hint { display: none !important; }
.skip-intro { display: none !important; }
.replay-scene { display: none !important; }
.judge-toggle { display: none !important; }
.judge-footer { display: none !important; }
"""


async def record_pass_a():
    """Cold open + BLOCK scene. ~32s.

    Scene-0 plays its built-in 10s sequence (chrome opens, URL types,
    Gemini loads, prompt types via QUERY constant). Then submit → scene 1
    (3 products visible). Then we directly invoke runScene2b for the BLOCK.
    """
    async with async_playwright() as pw:
        browser = await pw.chromium.launch(headless=True)
        ctx = await browser.new_context(
            viewport={"width": W, "height": H},
            record_video_dir=str(OUT),
            record_video_size={"width": W, "height": H},
            device_scale_factor=1.0,
        )
        await ctx.add_init_script(f"""
          window.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', () => {{
            const s = document.createElement('style');
            s.textContent = {HIDE_CHROME_CSS!r};
            document.head.appendChild(s);
          }});
        """)
        page = await ctx.new_page()
        await page.goto(f"{BASE}/demo?intro=block&judge=1", wait_until="networkidle")
        await asyncio.sleep(0.5)

        await page.evaluate("if (window.runToken !== undefined) runToken += 1;")
        await asyncio.sleep(0.3)
        await page.evaluate("playScene(0)")
        # Scene-0 runs ~10s (URL types, Gemini loads, prompt types, submit armed).
        print("[A] T=0.0 scene 0")
        await asyncio.sleep(11.0)

        # Submit → scene 1. Scene 1 native is 1.3s (show-products + ping).
        await page.evaluate("document.getElementById('s0-submit').click()")
        print("[A] T=11.0 submit → scene 1")
        # Hold scene-1 longer (it's "what the agent would have shipped")
        # so beat 2 VO has visual room. Beat 2 ends at 18.35s — keep
        # scene-1 visible until then.
        await asyncio.sleep(7.5)

        # Directly skip scene-2 PASS for the BLOCK-first storyboard.
        await page.evaluate("""
          (() => {
            scenes[2].classList.add('complete');
            document.getElementById('s3-status').textContent = 'VERIFIED';
            runToken += 1;
            runScene2b(runToken);
          })();
        """)
        print("[A] T=18.5 runScene2b BLOCK")
        # scene-2b native: ~4.1s card animation, then BLOCKED.
        # VO beats 4+5 cover 47-57s in the final mix, so scene-2b
        # capture needs to last ~24s minimum after the title card cut.
        await asyncio.sleep(24.5)
        print("[A] T=43.0 hold replacement copy")
        await asyncio.sleep(2.0)

        await ctx.close()
        await browser.close()

        # rename the recording
        webms = sorted(OUT.glob("page@*.webm"))
        if not webms:
            return None
        final = OUT / "passA.webm"
        if final.exists():
            final.unlink()
        webms[-1].rename(final)
        print(f"[A] saved -> {final}")
        return final


async def record_pass_b():
    """Verified PASS scene + Gemini recommendation + vendor checkout. ~46s.

    Loads /demo (default hip-joint prompt), jumps to scene-2 cold (running
    the full PASS animation), continues to scene-3 recommendation, then
    scene-4 vendor + autonomous cursor checkout.
    """
    async with async_playwright() as pw:
        browser = await pw.chromium.launch(headless=True)
        ctx = await browser.new_context(
            viewport={"width": W, "height": H},
            record_video_dir=str(OUT),
            record_video_size={"width": W, "height": H},
            device_scale_factor=1.0,
        )
        await ctx.add_init_script(f"""
          window.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', () => {{
            const s = document.createElement('style');
            s.textContent = {HIDE_CHROME_CSS!r};
            document.head.appendChild(s);
          }});
        """)
        page = await ctx.new_page()
        # Default (hip-joint) prompt + judge mode on
        await page.goto(f"{BASE}/demo?judge=1", wait_until="networkidle")
        await asyncio.sleep(0.5)

        # Jump straight to scene-2 (skip 0 + 1).
        # CRITICAL: scene-2's runScene2 has an auto-advance to scene-2b
        # at the tail. To prevent that, we bump runToken WHILE the
        # verified frame holds (token-check kills the auto-advance).
        await page.evaluate("runToken += 1; playScene(2);")
        print("[B] T=0.0 scene 2 PASS")
        # Scene-2 plays bento ~3s + verified state. Hold the VERIFIED
        # frame for 14s more (beat 6 VO is 18s of "mesh clears the real
        # ones" + signed bundle + chain anchor). Block runScene2 from
        # auto-advancing into scene-2b by bumping runToken at 4s.
        await asyncio.sleep(4.0)
        await page.evaluate("runToken += 1;")  # cancel auto-advance into 2b
```

#### `corpus/aafco-pf7-substantiation.txt` — 32 lines

```text
# AAFCO PF7 — Substantiation of Claims (public-side summary)

The Association of American Feed Control Officials (AAFCO) Model Regulations PF7 requires that claims made on pet food and supplement labels be substantiated with scientifically valid evidence. PF7 governs general substantiation requirements for all label claims and advertising claims for animal feed and supplement products.

## Key requirements

1. Claims must be truthful and not misleading.
2. Substantiation must consist of competent and reliable scientific evidence.
3. The level of substantiation required depends on the specificity and disease-related nature of the claim.
4. Disease prevention or treatment claims require evidence approaching the level of drug substantiation (typically falls under FDA-CVM jurisdiction, not AAFCO).
5. Structure-function claims (e.g., "supports joint health," "promotes calm demeanor") require credible scientific evidence specific to the species, but typically not full clinical trials.

## "Veterinarian-recommended" claim

AAFCO requires that "veterinarian-recommended" or "vet-recommended" claims be backed by a statistically significant, professionally sound survey of veterinarians. Surveys must be representative of the veterinary community making the recommendation. Marketing the product with this claim without survey evidence violates PF7.

## "Veterinarian-formulated" claim

AAFCO permits "vet-formulated" claims when at least one veterinarian was involved in the formulation of the product. The brand must have documentation of veterinary involvement (consulting agreement, product development records, signed attestation).

## Ingredient-based claims

Claims about specific ingredients (chondroitin, glucosamine, omega-3, etc.) must be supported by credible scientific evidence in the target species or closely related species. Extrapolation from human or rodent studies alone is insufficient for canine or feline efficacy claims absent confirmatory species-specific evidence.

## Implications for pet supplement brands

- "Supports joint health" requires species-specific scientific evidence (canine or feline depending on target).
- Vet-formulated requires documented veterinary involvement.
- Vet-recommended requires statistically valid vet survey.
- All claims must be in the advertiser's possession before making them.

Source: AAFCO Model Regulations Section PF7 (public-side summary, no member-only content).
```

#### `corpus/ftc-16cfr-255-0.txt` — 21 lines

```text
# 16 CFR § 255.0 - Purpose and Definitions

## (a) Purpose
The Guides interpret FTC Act Section 5 regarding endorsements and testimonials in advertising. They provide "the basis for voluntary compliance with the law by advertisers and endorsers." Practices conflicting with these Guides may trigger corrective FTC action if the Commission determines they violate the statute. The Guides outline general evaluation principles with illustrative examples, though they don't address every possible endorsement scenario.

## (b) Endorsement Definition
An endorsement is "any advertising, marketing, or promotional message for a product that consumers are likely to believe reflects the opinions, beliefs, findings, or experiences of a party other than the sponsoring advertiser." Forms include verbal statements, social media tags, demonstrations, and use of names, signatures, or likenesses.

## (c) Endorsements and Testimonials
The Commission treats endorsements and testimonials identically for enforcement purposes.

## (d) Product Definition
"Product" encompasses any product, service, brand, company, or industry.

## (e) Expert Definition
An expert possesses "knowledge of a particular subject, which knowledge is superior to what ordinary individuals generally acquire."

## (f) Clear and Conspicuous
This means disclosures are "difficult to miss (i.e., easily noticeable) and easily understandable by ordinary consumers," appearing in relevant communication modes and remaining unavoidable and uncontradicted.

Source: 16 CFR Part 255, FTC Endorsement Guides (2023 update). Federal regulation, public domain.
```

#### `corpus/ftc-16cfr-255-1.txt` — 23 lines

```text
# 16 CFR § 255.1 - General Considerations

(a) Endorsements must reflect the honest opinions, findings, beliefs, or experience of the endorser. Furthermore, an endorsement may not convey any express or implied representation that would be deceptive if made directly by the advertiser.

(b) An advertisement need not present an endorser's message in the exact words of the endorser unless the advertisement represents that it is presenting the endorser's exact words, such as through the use of quotation marks. However, the endorsement may not be presented out of context or reworded so as to distort in any way the endorser's opinion or experience with the product. An advertiser may use an endorsement of an expert or celebrity only so long as it has good reason to believe that the endorser continues to subscribe to the views presented. An advertiser may satisfy this obligation by securing the endorser's views at reasonable intervals where reasonableness will be determined by such factors as new information about the performance or effectiveness of the product, a material alteration in the product, changes in the performance of competitors' products, and the advertiser's contract commitments.

(c) When the advertisement represents that the endorser uses the endorsed product, the endorser must have been a bona fide user of it at the time the endorsement was given. Additionally, the advertiser may continue to run the advertisement only so long as it has good reason to believe that the endorser remains a bona fide user of the product.

(d) Advertisers are subject to liability for misleading or unsubstantiated statements made through endorsements or for failing to disclose unexpected material connections between themselves and their endorsers. An advertiser may be liable for a deceptive endorsement even when the endorser is not liable. Advertisers should:

(1) Provide guidance to their endorsers on the need to ensure that their statements are not misleading and to disclose unexpected material connections;

(2) Monitor their endorsers' compliance; and

(3) Take action sufficient to remedy non-compliance and prevent future non-compliance. While not a safe harbor, good faith and effective guidance, monitoring, and remedial action should reduce the incidence of deceptive claims and reduce an advertiser's odds of facing a Commission enforcement action.

(e) Endorsers may be liable for statements made in the course of their endorsements, such as when an endorser makes a representation that the endorser knows or should know to be deceptive, including when an endorser falsely represents that they personally used a product. Also, an endorser who is not an expert may be liable for misleading or unsubstantiated representations regarding a product's performance or effectiveness, such as when the representations are inconsistent with the endorser's personal experience or were not made or approved by the advertiser and go beyond the scope of the endorser's personal experience. Endorsers may also be liable for failing to disclose unexpected material connections between themselves and an advertiser, such as when an endorser creates and disseminates endorsements without such disclosures.

(f) Advertising agencies, public relations firms, review brokers, reputation management companies, and other similar intermediaries may be liable for their roles in creating or disseminating endorsements containing representations that they know or should know are deceptive.

(g) The use of an endorsement with the image or likeness of a person other than the actual endorser is deceptive if it misrepresents a material attribute of the endorser.

Source: 16 CFR Part 255, FTC Endorsement Guides (2023 update). Federal regulation, public domain.
```

#### `corpus/ftc-16cfr-255-2.txt` — 13 lines

```text
# 16 CFR § 255.2 - Consumer Endorsements

(a) Substantiation Requirement: Advertisements using consumer endorsements must be supported by adequate substantiation. The advertiser must possess competent and reliable scientific evidence to support claims, just as if making them directly without endorsements. "Consumer endorsements themselves are not competent and reliable scientific evidence."

(b) Representativeness of Experience: When endorsements depict a central product attribute, they're interpreted as representing typical consumer results. If the endorser's experience isn't representative, the ad must "clearly and conspicuously disclose the generally expected performance" with adequate substantiation.

(c) Actual Consumers: Ads claiming to feature "actual consumers" must use real consumers in audio and video, or "clearly and conspicuously disclose that the persons in such advertisements are not actual consumers."

(d) Review Manipulation: Advertisers must not take actions "that have the effect of distorting or otherwise misrepresenting what consumers think of their products" through review suppression, boosting, or editing.

(e) Examples include eleven illustrative scenarios covering fake reviews, inadequate disclaimers, misleading rating systems, and coercive practices against reviewers.

Source: 16 CFR Part 255, FTC Endorsement Guides (2023 update). Federal regulation, public domain.
```

#### `corpus/ftc-16cfr-255-3.txt` — 30 lines

```text
# 16 CFR § 255.3 - Expert Endorsements

(a) When an advertisement claims expertise, the endorser's qualifications must actually provide that expertise regarding the endorsement message.

(b) Expert endorsers may consider factors outside their expertise (taste, price), but must demonstrate actual expertise through examination or testing comparable to standards in their field. Product evaluations must be as extensive as experts with similar credentials would conduct. When comparisons are implied, they must have occurred, with conclusions that the endorsed product equals or surpasses competitors' products on relevant consumer-available features. If superiority is conveyed, it must be factually established.

(c) Examples:

(1) An automobile engineer endorsement implies professional training in automobile design and performance. A chemical engineer's endorsement would be deceptive.

(2) A doctor endorsing hearing aids implies audiology expertise. Without such expertise, disclosure of limitations is required.

(3) "American Institute of Science" approval implies independent testing. If established by manufacturers or lacking valid testing, endorsement is deceptive.

(4) Hospital selection based on packaging unavailable to consumers is deceptive without consumer disclosure.

(5) Commercial cleaning service president endorsing cleansers represents superior consumer knowledge, requiring actual competitor experience and documented performance equality or superiority.

(6) Medical doctor claims require appropriate scientific evidence; consumer letters or animal studies alone constitute deception, making both advertiser and endorser liable.

## Implications for veterinary endorsements

For pet supplements claiming "veterinarian endorsed" or "vet-formulated":
- The veterinarian must have actual expertise in the relevant claim domain (e.g., clinical nutrition for joint health claims).
- Product evaluation must be as extensive as veterinary experts with comparable credentials would conduct.
- If comparison claims are implied or stated, those comparisons must have occurred with documented results.
- Consumer letters and animal studies alone are insufficient substantiation for medical claims.
- Both the brand and the veterinarian endorser can be liable for unsubstantiated claims.

Source: 16 CFR Part 255, FTC Endorsement Guides (2023 update). Federal regulation, public domain.
```

#### `corpus/ftc-16cfr-255-5.txt` — 25 lines

```text
# 16 CFR § 255.5 - Disclosure of Material Connections

(a) Core Requirement: When an endorser has a connection to a product seller that could materially affect credibility, and audiences wouldn't reasonably expect it, disclosure is required. The regulation defines material connections broadly: "Material connections can include a business, family, or personal relationship" as well as monetary payments, free products, early access, or other benefits.

The disclosure must "clearly communicate the nature of the connection sufficiently for consumers to evaluate its significance," though complete details aren't necessary.

(b) Fourteen Illustrative Examples cover scenarios such as:

- Funded research: Drug companies must disclose when they fund studies cited in advertisements
- Celebrity compensation: Standard commercial payments typically don't require disclosure, but unusual arrangements (equity stakes, ongoing royalties) do
- Medical endorsements: Healthcare influencers must disclose paid spokesperson relationships
- Social media posts: Influencers receiving free products must disclose the arrangement
- Employee endorsements: Company employees promoting products online must reveal their employment relationship
- Incentivized reviews: Programs paying consumers for reviews require clear disclosure of compensation
- Affiliate links: Bloggers earning commissions from product links must disclose this arrangement

## Implications for pet brand endorsements

For pet supplements:
- A veterinarian on retainer with a brand must disclose the relationship.
- "Vet-recommended" or "vet-formulated" claims with material connections require disclosure.
- Influencers receiving free pet products must disclose the arrangement.
- Funded clinical studies on pet products cited in advertising must disclose the funding source.

Source: 16 CFR Part 255, FTC Endorsement Guides (2023 update). Federal regulation, public domain.
```

#### `corpus/nasc-quality-seal-public.txt` — 32 lines

```text
# NASC Quality Seal Program — Public-Side Summary

The National Animal Supplement Council (NASC) operates a quality assurance program for the animal supplement industry. The NASC Quality Seal is awarded to member brands meeting the program's requirements.

## Public-side program requirements

1. **Biennial Independent Third-Party Audit:** NASC members must pass an independent on-site audit every two years covering manufacturing, quality control, recordkeeping, and labeling practices.

2. **Written Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs):** Members must maintain documented SOPs covering all manufacturing and quality processes.

3. **Adverse Event Reporting (AER) System:** Members must operate an AER system to track consumer-reported issues. NASC aggregates AER data across the industry to identify safety signals.

4. **Labeling Compliance:** Members must conform to NASC labeling guidelines, which align with AAFCO Model Regulations and FDA-CVM expectations for non-drug animal products.

5. **Random Product Testing for Label Accuracy:** NASC contracts independent laboratories to test member products for label accuracy (active ingredient quantities, absence of contaminants).

## What NASC does NOT certify

The NASC Quality Seal is a manufacturing-quality and labeling-compliance program. It does NOT certify:

- Clinical efficacy of supplement health claims.
- Substantiation of "supports joint health" or similar structure-function claims.
- Veterinary endorsement validity.
- FTC §255 endorsement substantiation requirements.

Claims-side substantiation is the brand's separate responsibility under FTC §255 (federal trade regulation) and AAFCO PF7 (state feed regulation).

## Industry coverage

NASC reports having approximately 300 audited member brands as of 2026. The animal supplement industry includes thousands of total brands; the NASC seal represents a subset of the most quality-conscious manufacturers.

Source: NASC Quality Seal Program (public-side summary from NASC.cc).
```
